company_setup: Domestic registration through de facto Ministry of Commerce/ACCI; foreign investment and international payments are severely constrained by sanctions and banking de-risking. Diaspora founders typically incorporate abroad (Delaware via Stripe Atlas, Estonia e-Residency).
summary: Since August 2021 the Taliban de facto authorities govern; the government is not internationally recognised, international banking is heavily constrained and women face severe restrictions on work and education. Startup activity is minimal and mostly diaspora-led or donor-supported.
notes: As of 2026-10-20. Taliban de facto rule, sanctions and banking restrictions; international VC effectively unavailable. AISA (investment agency) site did not resolve. Check sanctions compliance before any transaction.

startup_visa: none (startup grant is open to foreign individuals and digital nomads, but no dedicated startup visa verified)
company_setup: SHPK (LLC) registered with the National Business Center (QKB) online via e-Albania; foreigners can own 100%; registration typically within a day at minimal fee.
summary: Young ecosystem centred on Tirana, supported by the 2022 startup law and a state startup grant scheme (Startup Albania). Strong diaspora and outsourcing links; private VC is scarce and mostly regional.
notes: Startup Albania portal is JavaScript-rendered; second 2026 call dates unconfirmed. Few local accelerators/VCs could be verified with available tools.

company_setup: SARL/SPA via CNRC; foreign ownership rules eased in 2020 (51/49 lifted for most sectors); labelled startups get tax benefits.
summary: Large, under-digitised market; since 2020 the state has built a startup framework (startup label, Algerian Startup Fund) centred in Algiers.
notes: Algeria Venture accelerator site unreachable; omitted.

startup_visa: none (active residence for entrepreneurs requires business plan and foreign investment authorisation)
company_setup: SL (Societat Limitada) with foreign investment authorisation from the Government; registration via tramits.ad; a few weeks.
summary: Pyrenean microstate with low taxes (10% corporate) attracting digital entrepreneurs and content creators; small ecosystem supported by Andorra Business (Actua) and the University of Andorra.
notes: Andorra Business site blocks automated fetch; no accelerator or VC verified. Not in EU/Horizon Europe.

startup_visa: none; private investment via AIPEX, https://www.aipex.gov.ao/PortalAIPEX/
company_setup: Lda via Guiche Unico da Empresa (GUE), possible in days; foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Luanda-centred, oil-dependent economy with a young, Portuguese-speaking ecosystem; state SME institute INAPEM and the development bank BDA support entrepreneurs.

company_setup: IBC or local company under the Companies Act; foreign ownership allowed. Citizenship by Investment can be obtained through business investment.
summary: Very small ecosystem; the economy rests on tourism and financial services. The Investment Authority offers SME services; there are no local accelerators or VCs.
notes: OECS member, not an IDB borrowing member; regional support comes via CDB, Compete Caribbean, OECS and Caribbean Export. OECS Youth Empowerment Project small grants (US$5k) closed 2026-08-14. A Nomad Digital Residence remote-work visa exists; its official URL was not verified.

startup_visa: none (no startup visa; digital nomad visa and standard residence routes via Dirección Nacional de Migraciones)
company_setup: Typical entity S.A. or S.R.L. (S.A.S. availability restricted in practice); foreigners can incorporate but need a CDI/CUIT and local legal domicile; 1–2 months. Many VC-backed startups use a Delaware holdco.
summary: Talent-rich ecosystem centred on Buenos Aires and Córdoba that produced MercadoLibre, Globant, Ualá, Auth0 and Despegar. Strong in software, fintech, agtech and biotech, but macro volatility and capital controls shape fundraising.
notes: National startup programs were cut back in 2024–2026; Fondo Semilla/Fondo Expansión no longer active as of 2026. Provincial funds (e.g. Córdoba Semilla/Triple F up to ARS 40M, closed 2026-07-08; Río Negro; San Juan) are the main public seed sources but their official URLs could not be verified, so they are omitted. Wayra Argentina site has an expired certificate and is not listed among Wayra hubs. ~ARS 1,400/US$ (volatile).

startup_visa: No startup visa. Many nationalities are visa-free for 180 days; e-visa at https://evisa.mfa.am/
company_setup: LLC registered online via the e-register in 1-2 days, with free state registration. Foreigners can register through a representative. A turnover-tax regime is available for small businesses.
summary: Strong engineering talent base in Yerevan with globally known startups such as Picsart, Krisp and ServiceTitan (co-founded by Armenians). Supported by EIF, FAST, the Ministry of High-Tech Industry and an active diaspora angel scene.
notes: Oct 2026: FAST's site blocks automated access, so its program terms and deadlines are unverified. Hive Ventures was left out (domain not confirmed).

startup_visa: National Innovation Visa (subclass 858, permanent, invitation-only via EOI; covers exceptional entrepreneurs), https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/national-innovation-visa-858
company_setup: Proprietary limited company (Pty Ltd) registered online with ASIC in about a day (fee about A$600). Needs at least one director ordinarily resident in Australia, so foreigners usually appoint a local director.
summary: Largest startup ecosystem in Oceania, centred on Sydney and Melbourne with growing Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide hubs. Strong in SaaS, fintech, healthtech and deep tech; global outcomes include Atlassian, Canva, Afterpay and Airwallex.
notes: As of 2026-10-20: Industry Growth Program paused to new applications since 12 May 2026; EMDG Round 4 closed pending the 2026 review; R&DTI changes announced in the 2026-27 Budget take effect from 1 July 2028. LaunchVic and Breakthrough Victoria merged into Innovation Victoria on 1 July 2026. Techstars Sydney closed after NSW funding ended (no 2026 program), and the Sydney School of Entrepreneurship wound down in August 2025, so both are left out. The ICON 2026 date comes from a CBRIN article; the official page rate-limited the fetch. Antler AU cheque size is not published.

startup_visa: Red-White-Red Card for start-up founders (min. €30k capital, 50% equity share, points test), https://www.migration.gv.at/en/types-of-immigration/permanent-immigration/start-up-founders/
company_setup: GmbH (€10k minimum capital) or FlexCo (flexible company, since 2024); founding via notary or online via USP; 1–3 weeks.
summary: Compact ecosystem centred on Vienna, with Graz, Linz and Innsbruck as secondary hubs. Strong public funding via aws and FFG; strengths in deep tech, fintech, crypto and B2B software; notable companies include Bitpanda, GoStudent and Tricentis.
notes: aws Preseed amounts/call windows not shown on the overview page; FFG pages block automated reads (Cloudflare). EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

company_setup: LLC registered via the State Tax Service e-registration or ASAN centres in about 1-3 days. Foreigners can own 100%. A KOBIA Startup Certificate gives a 3-year exemption on income from innovation activity, and Texnopark residents get 10-year tax benefits.
summary: Baku-centred ecosystem led by the state Innovation and Digital Development Agency (IDDA), which absorbed the former Innovation Agency, and the SMB Development Agency (KOBIA). IDDA reports 750+ startups supported, but the private VC base is small.
notes: Oct 2026: no open IDDA startup call was found in its news feed. White Hill Capital announced a US$5m fund with IDDA in Sep 2025, but there is no standalone site. KOBIA's grant page shows old dates, so check the current round. PASHA Investments is private equity (typed family_office as the closest fit).

company_setup: IBC or domestic company. Foreign ownership in some sectors needs Bahamas Investment Authority approval; reserved sectors are for Bahamians. Registration takes about a week or more.
summary: Small ecosystem in Nassau built around the government's SBDC/Access Accelerator and the Bahamas Entrepreneurial Venture Fund. Digital-asset regulation (DARE Act) has drawn fintech and crypto firms; the University of The Bahamas runs the UB Ignite incubator.
notes: SBDC grant/loan amounts are not published online; contact the SBDC. In 2026 UB Ignite ran a fintech pitch with OKX Bahamas (114 applicants).

startup_visa: Golden Residency (investor/talent categories); no dedicated startup visa
company_setup: WLL or SPC via Sijilat portal; 100% foreign ownership in most sectors; can be done in days, largely remotely.
summary: Compact, regulator-friendly hub for fintech (CBB sandbox, Bahrain FinTech Bay) with strong Tamkeen subsidies and the Al Waha fund of funds.
notes: Al Waha Fund of Funds site returned errors; omitted. Flat6Labs Bahrain activity not verified.

company_setup: Private limited company via RJSC online; foreign investors register with BIDA; 100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors; about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Dhaka-centred ecosystem with large consumer market; fintech (bKash, Nagad), logistics and e-commerce lead. Government supports startups via ICT Division (iDEA) and the state VC Startup Bangladesh Limited.
notes: As of 2026-10-20. Startup Bangladesh Limited's site (startupbangladesh.vc redirects to startupbangladesh.gov.bd) returned errors during checks; verify before relying on it. Political transition since Aug 2024 may affect government schemes.

company_setup: Private company registered with CAIPO, mostly online; foreigners can own 100%. Typically 1-2 weeks.
summary: Small, policy-led ecosystem. FutureBarbados (incubator Catapult, accelerator Flight), Export Barbados and TEN Habitat support founders. The IDB is preparing a pre-seed venture studio. The Welcome Stamp has drawn remote workers.
notes: IDB project BA-G1009 (US$1.25M, in preparation in 2026) plans a pre-seed venture studio for digital startups. The FutureBarbados site appears not updated since 2023; check for current calls.

company_setup: LLC (OOO); IT companies can apply for Hi-Tech Park residency (0% profit tax and VAT, 9% salary income tax, 13% in 2023-2027). Foreign founders face sanctions, banking and payment restrictions; relocated founders typically incorporate in Poland, Lithuania or the US.
summary: Historically strong IT outsourcing and product hub in Minsk (EPAM, Wargaming, Viber, MSQRD/Flo founders), but since 2020-2022 large parts of the tech workforce and many startups have relocated to Poland, Lithuania, Georgia and elsewhere. Remaining activity is concentrated around the Hi-Tech Park.
notes: Sanctions: Belarus is under extensive EU, UK and US sanctions (since 2020-2022, tightened after its role in the invasion of Ukraine). Western VCs, accelerators and most international payment rails are effectively unavailable; Belarusian nationals are excluded from some EU programmes (e.g. EBRD-backed Bridge to Scale). Not eligible for EIC/Horizon Europe. RBF Ventures was set up in 2016 with Russia's RVC. Many well-known Belarusian startups now operate from abroad; include them under their new countries.

startup_visa: none (non-EU founders need a regional professional card / self-employed permit)
company_setup: SRL/BV with no minimum capital but a mandatory financial plan; notarial deed and KBO/BCE registration; about 1–2 weeks.
summary: Mid-sized ecosystem split across Flanders (Ghent, Leuven, Antwerp), Brussels and Wallonia, with regional funding agencies. Strengths in biotech, semiconductors (imec), B2B SaaS and fintech; notable companies include Collibra, Odoo, Showpad and Deliverect.
notes: Funding is regional (Flanders/Brussels/Wallonia). Start it @KBC fall 2026 cohort deadline was 14 Sep 2026; next intake date not yet published. VLAIO and PMV sites block automated checks but are the official domains. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

company_setup: Local company or IBC via the Belize Companies and Corporate Affairs Registry (online); foreign ownership allowed; about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Micro ecosystem. Support comes from BELTRAIDE (incl. SBDC Belize), BEEP seed grants and the Development Finance Corporation, plus Caribbean and Central American regional programmes (CDB, CABEI, RevUP).
notes: BEEP's 2026 cohort: 22 startups each got BZ$5,000 (July 2026). RevUP ran training for Belizean entrepreneurs.

company_setup: OHADA SARL/SAS via APIEx one-stop shop, largely online (within days, low fees). ADPME runs a digital SME platform.
summary: Small but government-driven ecosystem around Cotonou and Sèmè City innovation campus; World Bank-funded SME and youth programmes (RISE, Next Impact).
notes: Fem'IMA 2026 (women entrepreneurs, Sèmè City) closed 2026-04-12. Benin is in Choose Africa 2 priority countries.

startup_visa: none nationally; Gelephu Mindfulness City SAR runs its own business and residency framework
company_setup: Domestic firms register via MoICE; FDI governed by FDI Policy with sector restrictions and minimum project costs, so most small startups are Bhutanese-owned.
summary: Very small ecosystem centred on Thimphu; government-led support via MoICE and Thimphu TechPark. Gelephu Mindfulness City is a new special administrative region targeting investors.
notes: As of 2026-10-20. startup.bt is suspended. No VCs active locally.

company_setup: SRL or S.A. registered with SEPREC plus NIT tax ID; foreigners can own; about 2-4 weeks.
summary: Nascent ecosystem (IDB 2026 diagnostic) in Santa Cruz and La Paz, maturing over 2022-25 with new local VC (Escalatec), angels and accelerators (Solydes/Acelerate). The state bank BDP runs a Fondo STARTUP.
notes: FX controls and a dollar shortage (2024-26) complicate foreign investment and repatriation.

company_setup: d.o.o. registered separately in the Federation of BiH, Republika Srpska or Brcko District; minimum capital about BAM 1,000 in FBiH and BAM 1 in RS, typically 1-4 weeks with notary and court registration. Foreigners can be sole owners; no remote incorporation. FIPA assists foreign investors.
summary: Small ecosystem concentrated in Sarajevo, Banja Luka, Tuzla and Mostar, built around IT outsourcing and a few technology parks. Local VC is very thin; startups rely on regional Western Balkans funds, EBRD and donor programmes, and diaspora networks.
notes: As of 2026-10-20: no domestic VC fund confirmed active; regional funds (SCV, 5Q, StartLabs, Silicon Gardens) cover BiH. Star Venture showed no open Western Balkans call. FMRPO 2026 credit call deadline not readable. Diaspora route: many founders incorporate in Croatia, Slovenia or the US.

startup_visa: none; investor/residence permits via BITC, https://www.bitc.co.bw/
company_setup: Private company registered online with CIPA; foreigners can incorporate; some sectors reserved for citizens.
summary: Small, stable ecosystem in Gaborone backed by the state: Botswana Innovation Hub, CEDA finance and LEA SME support; diamond-dependent economy pushing digital diversification.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Botswana Innovation Hub site sits behind a captcha.

startup_visa: Residence authorization for investment in innovation/startups (Ministério da Justiça, CNIg rules), https://www.gov.br/mj/pt-br/assuntos/seus-direitos/migracoes/autorizacao-de-residencia
company_setup: Typical entity Ltda or S.A. (Sociedade Anônima for VC rounds); foreigners need a CPF and a resident administrator or attorney; registration via Redesim/Junta Comercial in about 1–4 weeks. Many VC-backed startups use a Cayman/Delaware holdco.
summary: Largest ecosystem in Latin America, centred on São Paulo with hubs in Florianópolis, Belo Horizonte, Rio and Recife. Home to Nubank, iFood, QuintoAndar, Ebanx and other unicorns; strongest in fintech, agtech and SaaS.
notes: Finep subsidy calls in 2026 (Mais Inovação) mostly closed; several required firms with 3 years of balance sheets. BNDES Garagem 3rd edition runs to 2028 with yearly calls; 2026 dates not yet published. FAPESP PIPE amounts approximate, check Valores page. Exchange rate ~R$5.4/US$.

company_setup: Private company limited by shares registered via the Registry of Companies (ROCBN, under the Ministry of Finance and Economy); foreign ownership allowed in many sectors, with a resident director required.
summary: Small ecosystem focused on diversifying from oil and gas, led by the Brunei Economic Development Board (BEDB), which now runs DARe-era bootcamps, the iCentre incubator and Kontena Park.
notes: DARe programmes now appear under BEDB; dare.gov.bn returns 404. Grant amount comes from secondary reports.

startup_visa: Bulgaria Startup Visa: certificate for a high-tech/innovative project issued free by the Ministry of Innovation and Growth (30 days, via eNIMS), then D visa and residence permit, https://www.mig.government.bg/3263-issuance-of-a-sertificate-for-a-high-tech-and-or-innovative-project-startup-visa/?lang=en
company_setup: EOOD/OOD limited company in the Commercial Register; nominal minimum capital; foreigners can incorporate remotely via notarised power of attorney; about 1 week; 10% corporate tax.
summary: Sofia-centred ecosystem with strong software outsourcing roots and an active local VC scene seeded by EU-backed fund-of-funds programmes (about EUR 500M managed by local VC funds per BVCA). Bulgaria joined the euro area in January 2026.
notes: Fund of Funds Entrepreneurship Fund manager agreements were delayed by appeals in 2025; check which managers are investing. National Innovation Fund session timing for 2026/27 not confirmed. Eleven Ventures site (eleven.bg redirects to 11.me) blocked automated checks. EBRD Star Venture coverage of Bulgaria not confirmed, so omitted.

company_setup: OHADA SARL/SAS via Maison de l'Entreprise (CEFORE one-stop shop), typically within days. Diaspora/remote: incorporate abroad.
summary: Small Ouagadougou ecosystem with Orange Digital Centers (three by 2026) and BeoogoLab startup studio; insecurity limits investment.
notes: Military government; left ECOWAS (AES) in Jan 2025 but remains in UEMOA/CFA. Security risk deters foreign VC. La Fabrique site unreachable and omitted.

company_setup: SURL or SPRL via the one-stop shop of the Agence de Developpement du Burundi; foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Very small ecosystem in Bujumbura; donor-backed incubation (Orange Corners, Burundi Business Incubator) and a national development agency.

startup_visa: none (Remote Working Cabo Verde digital-nomad visa exists)
company_setup: Company via Casa do Cidadão / Empresa no Dia (same-day registration possible); foreigners may own 100%.
summary: Small, stable island economy positioning as a digital hub (TechPark CV in Praia) with public SME agency, venture-capital and guarantee companies.
notes: Digital-nomad visa site not verified.

company_setup: Private limited company registered online with the Ministry of Commerce (100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors); takes about 1–3 weeks. Many founders use a Singapore holding company.
summary: Small but growing ecosystem in Phnom Penh, with 235 startups recorded in 2025 and a National Strategy on Startup Development 2026–2030. Government support via Khmer Enterprise (MEF) and Techo Startup Center; corporate VC from Smart Axiata and Canadia.
notes: Khmer Enterprise site content did not load for verification; programme details come from partner pages.

company_setup: OHADA SARL/SAS via CFCE one-stop shop (online, about 72 hours).
summary: Bilingual ecosystem across Douala, Yaoundé and Buea (Silicon Mountain); strengths in fintech and edtech; CEMAC/CFA zone.
notes: ActivSpaces site under construction at time of check; omitted. Anglophone-region conflict affects Buea.

startup_visa: Start-up Visa Program paused since 1 Jan 2026 (final PR window for holders of 2025 commitment certificates closed 30 Jun 2026); IRCC plans a new high-impact start-up pilot with no launch date yet, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/start-visa.html
company_setup: Federal (CBCA) or provincial corporation; federal incorporation online via Corporations Canada (about CA$200, often same day). CBCA requires 25% resident Canadian directors; Ontario, BC and Quebec corporations do not. CCPC status unlocks the enhanced SR&ED refund.
summary: Large, well-funded ecosystem led by Toronto-Waterloo, Vancouver and Montreal, with growing hubs in Calgary, Ottawa and Halifax. Strong in AI (Vector, Mila, Amii), fintech and SaaS; notable successes include Shopify, Wealthsimple, Cohere and Clio.
notes: Start-up Visa paused since 1 Jan 2026 with a replacement pilot planned. IRAP is set to move into the new Canada Innovation Corporation by 2026-27. SDTC was wound down and is excluded. Techstars Toronto no longer appears among Techstars programs. The SR&ED CA$6M limit comes from Budget 2025 and was not confirmed on the CRA page. Web search budget ran out mid-batch, so some deadlines are 'unknown'.

company_setup: OHADA company via the Guichet Unique de Formalités des Entreprises in Bangui. Diaspora route: incorporate abroad.
summary: Fragile state with almost no formal startup ecosystem; activity limited to donor and pan-African programmes.
notes: Ongoing conflict; no national startup agency or Orange Digital Center site verified.

company_setup: OHADA company via ANIE one-stop shop in N'Djamena.
summary: Nascent N'Djamena ecosystem anchored by WenakLabs; government digital agency ADETIC; very limited capital.
notes: Political transition and regional insecurity.

startup_visa: Start-Up Chile participants get visa support; general route is the temporary residence visa, https://startupchile.org/
company_setup: Typical entity SpA; can be formed online in 1 day free via Empresa en un Día (tuempresaenundia.cl) but needs a RUT; foreigners can obtain a RUT via a local representative. Total cost under US$500.
summary: Compact, government-backed ecosystem centred on Santiago, known for Start-Up Chile and CORFO co-funding. Notable companies include NotCo, Betterfly, Fintual and Buk; strengths in fintech, foodtech, mining and climate tech.
notes: Start-Up Chile 2026 call closed 25 May 2026; the site says next applications open soon (no date). Semilla Inicia/Expande run as regional calls with differing dates. Ignite amount stated as CLP 30M or up to 50M by different sources. ~CLP 950/US$.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; founders use Z work, M business or R talent visas; some free-trade zones run talent schemes), https://en.nia.gov.cn
company_setup: Wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company registered with SAMR. Usually needs a local registered address and in-person or agent filings, so remote setup in practice goes through an agent. Under the 2024 Company Law, registered capital must be paid within 5 years. Takes about 1-3 months.
summary: World's second-largest startup ecosystem, centred on Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hangzhou, strong in AI, EVs, hardware, robotics and biotech. Many exits via STAR Market and Hong Kong listings. USD-fund activity has fallen since 2022 and RMB state-guided funds now dominate.
notes: As of Oct 2026, US outbound investment rules restrict US LPs and investors in AI, semiconductors and quantum, so most new money is RMB and state-guided. Government calls are mostly Chinese-only and published per city or district. Fund check sizes are rarely published. Web search was exhausted during research, so several entities were verified by direct site checks only.

startup_visa: none (no startup visa; Visa V digital nomad and Visa M/R investor routes via Cancillería, https://www.cancilleria.gov.co/)
company_setup: Typical entity S.A.S., registrable at the Cámara de Comercio in days; foreigners can be shareholders but need a passport/cédula de extranjería and RUT; about US$300–1,000.
summary: Fast-growing ecosystem led by Bogotá and Medellín; unicorns include Rappi, Habi and Addi. Strong in fintech, proptech and delivery, with active public support through iNNpulsa and Ruta N.
notes: iNNpulsa lists several calls as open in Oct 2026 but publishes dates per call page; amounts vary. Wayra no longer lists Colombia. Local VC list thin due to verification limits. ~COP 4,000/US$.

company_setup: Registration through the national investment promotion agency (ANPI) and commercial registry; most diaspora founders incorporate in France or Mauritius.
summary: Minimal startup ecosystem; economy relies on remittances, agriculture and fishing.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. No national investment agency or SME site could be confirmed live.

company_setup: OHADA SARL/SAS via the Guichet Unique de Création d'Entreprise (online, few days); ANAPI supports investors.
summary: Large, fast-growing Kinshasa scene (plus Goma, Lubumbashi) with hubs like Silikin Village and Ingenious City; 2022 startup law; fintech and edtech lead.
notes: Conflict in the east (North/South Kivu). Startup ordinance-law of 2022 provides label and tax incentives; official portal not verified.

startup_visa: none (digital nomad visa under Ley 10008 via Migracion: https://www.migracion.go.cr)
company_setup: Sociedad Anonima or SRL registered with the Registro Nacional (digital signature/notary); foreigners can own 100%; about 1-3 weeks.
summary: One of Central America's most developed ecosystems, around San Jose, built on multinational tech and life-science operations (CINDE). SBD funds seed capital through operators such as ParqueTec, Impact Hub and CAMTIC. Carao Ventures is the main local seed VC, and the Costa Rica Angels network launched in May 2026.
notes: CRC converted at ~500/US$. The SBD site blocks automated access, so check calls with each operator. The LEAPCR (IDB Lab, PCII, CRUSA, SBD) high-potential startup initiative was announced June 2026; no official page was found.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; Croatia offers a temporary stay permit for digital nomads, https://mup.gov.hr/aliens-281621/temporary-stay-of-digital-nomads-286853/286853)
company_setup: d.o.o. (min capital EUR 2,500) or simple j.d.o.o. (min EUR 1), registered via notary or the START/e-Tvrtka online system at the court register, typically a few days. Foreigners need a Croatian OIB tax number; online founding requires a qualified e-signature/eID.
summary: Fast-growing ecosystem led by Zagreb, with Rijeka, Split and Osijek as secondary hubs. Home to unicorns Infobip and Rimac and gaming studio Nanobit (sold to Stillfront); funding is driven by HAMAG-BICRO grants, HBOR-backed VC funds and regional VCs.
notes: As of 2026-10-20: HAMAG-BICRO listed the PoC first call and S3 process-innovation call (both posted 3 Aug 2026) as open, but amounts and closing dates were not readable. ZICER applications for the current cycle are closed.

company_setup: Mipyme (private SME) under Decree-Law 46/2021, approved by the Ministry of Economy and Planning. Foreigners cannot own mipymes; foreign investment goes through joint ventures or the Mariel ZED.
summary: Private MSMEs (mipymes) legal only since 2021 and now number in the thousands; tech startups are few and informal. The Havana Science and Technology Park incubates a small number of firms. No VC or startup funding market.
notes: US embargo and OFAC rules (as of Oct 2026) block most US investors, platforms and payments; international VC effectively unavailable. Cuba is not an IDB member. A UNDP/MEP entrepreneur training programme was reported in 2026, but no official page was confirmed.

startup_visa: Cyprus Start-up Visa scheme (Ministry of Finance/Invest Cyprus endorsement) for non-EU founders, https://www.investcyprus.org.cy/
company_setup: Private limited company (Ltd) via the Department of Registrar of Companies; no minimum capital in practice; typically via local lawyer, about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Limassol/Nicosia ecosystem boosted by tech relocation, fintech and gaming; 12.5% corporate tax and IP box. Public funding through the Research and Innovation Foundation (RIF) and Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy.
notes: No Cyprus VC fund verified (several candidate domains parked). RIF calls checked 2026-10-20.

startup_visa: Key and Scientific Personnel Programme for startups (CzechInvest), https://czechstartups.gov.cz/startup-viza/
company_setup: s.r.o. with CZK 1 minimum capital; requires notarial deed and trade licence, typically 1-3 weeks; foreigners can incorporate, often via proxy/notary.
summary: Prague and Brno hubs with strong engineering talent; exits and unicorns include Avast, Productboard, Rohlik and Mews. Active local VCs (Credo, Rockaway, Reflex, Presto) plus government support via CzechInvest, TACR and NRB.
notes: API agency site has moved (apiagentura.gov.cz); OP TAK call dates not verified. StartupYard investment terms not published on site.

company_setup: OHADA SARL or SAS via CEPICI one-stop shop (often within 24-48 hours, low fees); foreigners may own 100%. Startup Act label gives tax exemptions to majority-Ivorian startups.
summary: Abidjan is francophone West Africa's main hub with startups raising about US$33M in 2024 (Partech); strengths in fintech, e-commerce and agritech; Startup Act (Law 2023-901) in force since 2024.
notes: Startup label committee created Mar 2025 (Ministry of Digital Transition); no official label portal URL verified. Orange Fab CI season 10 demo day held 2026-10-08; next call expected. Agence CI PME site unreachable.

startup_visa: Start-up Denmark residence permit (business plan approved by expert panel), https://www.nyidanmark.dk/en-GB/You-want-to-apply/Work/Start-up-Denmark
company_setup: ApS (private limited) registered online at virk.dk within days; requires MitID or a representative; share capital paid in at registration.
summary: Copenhagen-centred ecosystem with strong life science (Novo Nordisk Foundation, BII), fintech, cleantech and robotics (Odense). Notable exits include Zendesk, Unity (origins), Trustpilot (IPO) and Pleo as a scaleup.
notes: Innovation Fund Denmark site now brands as Danmarks Innovationsfond; on 2026-10-20 it showed no open InnoBooster/Innofounder calls.

company_setup: SARL via the one-stop shop of the investment promotion agency; foreigners can own 100% in most sectors; free-zone companies are an option.
summary: Very small ecosystem centred on Djibouti City, built around logistics, ports and free zones; state economic development fund supports SMEs.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. No active local accelerator could be verified.

startup_visa: none (WIN 'Work in Nature' remote-work visa: https://windominica.gov.dm)
company_setup: Company under the Companies Act; foreign ownership allowed; CBI includes approved business projects.
summary: Micro ecosystem; finance comes from AID Bank and Invest Dominica Authority supports startups. The WIN (Work in Nature) visa targets remote workers.
notes: OECS member, not an IDB borrowing member; regional support comes via CDB, Compete Caribbean, OECS and Caribbean Export. OECS Youth Empowerment Project small grants (US$5k) closed 2026-08-14.

company_setup: SRL (sociedad de responsabilidad limitada) registered with the Chamber of Commerce and DGII; foreigners can own 100%; about 2-4 weeks.
summary: Fast-growing Caribbean hub centred on Santo Domingo. StartupBlink's 2026 index reported 52.9% ecosystem growth, the highest in the Caribbean. The Enlaces angel network, Promipyme's EmprendeLab and ProDominicana lead support, and regional VCs such as Carao are active.
notes: Startup World Cup DR national round was held 2026-10-13. The Santo Domingo FI chapter page was not enrolling; the Caribbean virtual cohort covers DR.

startup_visa: none (digital nomad visa via Cancilleria: https://www.cancilleria.gob.ec)
company_setup: SAS (sociedad por acciones simplificada) registered online with the Superintendencia de Companias in about 1-3 days at low cost; foreigners can be shareholders.
summary: Ecosystem centred on Quito, Guayaquil and Cuenca. Its first unicorn is Kushki (payments). Endeavor Ecuador, AEI, ConQuito (FonQuito seed fund), EPICO and Prendho support founders, and BuenTrip and IMPAQTO invest. The IDB GET Forum was held in Quito in Oct 2026.
notes: Uses the US dollar. Ecuador's regulation is often cited as a VC deterrent (2025). The CREAS impact fund closed in 2023.

startup_visa: none dedicated; investor residency via GAFI
company_setup: LLC or JSC via GAFI one-stop shop; 100% foreign ownership allowed; 1-3 weeks; many founders also use Delaware/UAE holdcos.
summary: Africa's top-3 startup market (Cairo, Alexandria) with strong fintech, logistics and e-commerce; notable startups Fawry (listed), MNT-Halan, Swvl. FX devaluations 2023-24 hit valuations.
notes: ITAC CFP page lists Sep 1 - Oct 29 without year; assumed 2026.

startup_visa: none (Freedom Visa: residency/citizenship for US$1M+ investment in BTC/USDT, https://www.freedomvisa.com)
company_setup: Sociedad Anonima de Capital Variable registered via the online one-stop shop (MiEmpresa/CNR); foreigners can own 100%; about 1-3 weeks.
summary: Small ecosystem in San Salvador that the government markets as a tech hub (bitcoin law, Freedom Visa). CoreNest launched a US$25M accelerator fund, Impact Hub San Salvador runs investment-readiness programmes, and it hosts a Startup World Cup round.
notes: Startupbootcamp announced plans (2025) to invest up to US$3.5M in 30 Salvadoran startups, but no official programme page was found. PROESA's site timed out in Oct 2026. Startup World Cup SV 2026 winner: DiiMO (July 2026).

company_setup: OHADA company via the Ventanilla Única Empresarial in Malabo; local partner often needed. Diaspora route: incorporate abroad.
summary: Essentially no formal startup ecosystem; oil-dependent economy; only pan-African and regional programmes apply.
notes: No national startup programmes verified.

company_setup: Private enterprise is tightly controlled by the state; foreigners rarely incorporate. Diaspora founders usually incorporate abroad.
summary: Essentially no formal startup ecosystem; private sector heavily restricted and internet access very limited.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. No national SME or investment agency website could be confirmed. Pan-African programmes say they are open to all 54 countries, but access in practice is limited.

startup_visa: Estonia Startup Visa (Startup Committee approval, up to 365 days long-stay, extendable), https://startupestonia.ee/startup-visa/
company_setup: OU (private limited), fully online via e-Residency or Estonian ID in about a day; minimal share capital; non-residents need a local contact person/registered address.
summary: Highest startup density in Europe, centred on Tallinn and Tartu; unicorns include Skype, Wise, Bolt, Pipedrive and Veriff. Strong digital government (e-Residency) and active Baltic VC scene.
notes: KredEx and Enterprise Estonia merged into EIS; kredex.ee redirects to eis.ee.

company_setup: Private company via the Registrar of Companies; EIPA one-stop shop helps foreign investors.
summary: Very small ecosystem around Mbabane and Manzini; SEDCO incubation and the Royal Science and Technology Park are the main supports.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Royal Science and Technology Park site unreachable.

startup_visa: none; investment permits via Ethiopian Investment Commission, https://investethiopia.gov.et/
company_setup: PLC registered with Ministry of Trade; foreign investors need EIC investment permit and minimum capital rules apply; some sectors reserved for nationals.
summary: Large, early ecosystem in Addis Ababa, opening up after telecom liberalisation (Safaricom Ethiopia) and fintech reforms; hubs include iceaddis; capital is scarce and FX controls apply.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. FX shortages and capital controls affect foreign VC. blueMoon's domain looked parked and was left out.

company_setup: Private company registered with the Registrar of Companies; foreign investors register with Investment Fiji. Online registration is available, but foreign investment registration takes a few weeks.
summary: The most developed startup scene in the Pacific islands, centred on Suva and Nadi, with fintech, tourism tech and agri-business activity backed by the Reserve Bank of Fiji's innovation work and donor programmes.
notes: Fiji Innovation Hub partners with Creative HQ (NZ), Mastercard and the Reserve Bank of Fiji. No local VC fund could be verified. The Ministry of Trade site, which runs the national MSME and young entrepreneur schemes, was unreachable (HTTP 500), so those schemes are left out. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

startup_visa: Finnish Startup Permit (Business Finland eligibility statement, then residence permit from Migri), https://www.startupinfinland.com/applying/
company_setup: Osakeyhtio (Oy), no minimum share capital; registered with PRH (Finnish Patent and Registration Office) online via YTJ, needs Finnish e-ID, otherwise paper or agent; about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Helsinki/Espoo-centred ecosystem anchored by Slush and Aalto, with Tampere, Oulu and Turku. Strong in gaming (Supercell, Rovio), deep tech (IQM), health and B2B SaaS; Business Finland is a major public funder.
notes: Business Finland startup instruments renamed (Sprint grant, Deep Tech Accelerator); amounts not shown on the summary page.

startup_visa: French Tech Visa for Founders (Passeport Talent, 4-year renewable; requires recognition by a partner incubator or public body), https://welcome.businessfrance.fr/simplanter-en-france/recruter-des-talents-internationaux/visas-et-titres-de-sejour/les-statuts-des-dirigeants-etrangers/french-tech-visa-for-founders/
company_setup: SAS is standard (from €1 capital); register online via the guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); typically 1–2 weeks; foreigners can incorporate remotely but need a French address and bank account.
summary: One of Europe's top two or three ecosystems, centred on Paris (Station F) with strong regional hubs in Lyon, Lille, Grenoble and Toulouse. Heavy public support via Bpifrance and France 2030; strengths in AI, deep tech, fintech and health; notable companies include Mistral AI, Doctolib, BlaBlaCar and Contentsquare.
notes: As of 2026-10-20 Bpifrance's i-Nov catalogue page says the offer is no longer available; next wave unconfirmed. Bpifrance Prêt d'amorçage also shows as no longer available. Station F programme pages list no fixed deadlines. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

company_setup: OHADA company via ANPI-Gabon one-stop shop (site not verified).
summary: Small Libreville ecosystem; sovereign fund FGIS is the main domestic investor; startup support mostly via donors and pan-African programmes.
notes: Transition government since 2023 coup, elections held 2025. ANPI-Gabon and Ogooué Labs sites unreachable.

company_setup: Company limited by shares via the Single Window Business Registry (MoTIE); GIEPA supports foreign investors.
summary: Small Banjul ecosystem; donor-backed (EU/ITC/Enabel) support for business support organisations; Gambia Angel Network for seed funding.
notes: Youth Empowerment Project (YEP) site unreachable; omitted.

startup_visa: No startup visa. Citizens of about 95 countries get visa-free stays of up to 1 year, https://www.evisa.gov.ge/GeoVisa/
company_setup: LLC or Individual Entrepreneur registered at the Public Service Hall (NAPR) in 1 day, possible through a representative with power of attorney. Small Business status gives 1% turnover tax; Virtual Zone status gives 0% CIT on foreign IT income.
summary: Tbilisi-centred ecosystem driven by the state agency GITA, which has funded 640+ startups with grants and runs accelerators with Plug and Play, Startupbootcamp, 500 Global and Founder Institute. Easy incorporation and low taxes attract relocating founders.
notes: Oct 2026: the Plug and Play deadline is 11 December (year inferred from the 2026-10-06 announcement). Enterprise Georgia (enterprise.gov.ge) was left out because its TLS certificate is invalid. Smart Capital and the Georgian angel networks were left out as unverified.

startup_visa: No dedicated startup visa; non-EU founders use the residence permit for self-employment (Sec. 21 AufenthG), https://www.make-it-in-germany.com/en/visa-residence/types/self-employment
company_setup: GmbH (€25k share capital, €12.5k paid in) or UG (from €1); notarised deed required, online notarisation possible since 2022; typically 1–4 weeks.
summary: Europe's second-largest ecosystem by VC raised, led by Berlin and Munich with strong hubs in Hamburg, Cologne and Leipzig. Strengths in deep tech, AI, mobility, industrial tech and fintech; notable successes include Celonis, N26, Delivery Hero and Personio.
notes: EXIST and other federal programmes are now under BMWE (renamed ministry). Most accelerator deadlines not published on official pages as of 2026-10-20. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

company_setup: Private company limited by shares via the Office of the Registrar of Companies (online, about 1-2 weeks). Foreign-owned firms register with GIPA and may face minimum foreign-capital rules.
summary: Accra is one of West Africa's top hubs, strong in fintech and agritech; MEST and a dense hub network; notable exits include Hubtel and mPharma growth rounds.
notes: Oct 2026: NEIP CEO announced transition to a Ghana Startup Agency; a Ghana startup bill is still in progress.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; Elevate Greece registry gives startup status)
company_setup: IKE (private company) from EUR 1 capital via the GEMI one-stop shop (businessportal.gr); online with Greek tax number; a few days.
summary: Athens and Thessaloniki ecosystem grown by EquiFund-backed VCs; exits include Workable growth, Blueground, Viva Wallet (JP Morgan stake) and Instashop. National startup registry via Elevate Greece.
notes: The Cube Athens and Found.ation domains no longer resolve; excluded. Uni.Fund site down at check time; excluded.

startup_visa: none (Danish immigration rules do not apply directly; Greenland work/residence permits via the Danish Agency for International Recruitment for Greenland)
company_setup: ApS or A/S under Greenlandic company law, registered in the Danish CVR via virk.dk; local address and Greenland tax liability needed for Nalik support.
summary: Very small Nuuk-centred economy (fishing, tourism, minerals). Startup support comes mainly from Nalik Ventures (the state business development company, apparently successor to Greenland Venture) and Danish/Nordic programs.
notes: greenlandventure.com is parked; venture.gl redirects to nalik.gl, so Greenland Venture appears to operate as Nalik Ventures (not confirmed on site). Danish programs (Innovation Fund Denmark, EIFO) generally require a Danish CVR company in Denmark proper; check eligibility.

company_setup: Company under the Companies Act via the Corporate Affairs and Intellectual Property Office; foreign ownership allowed. Grenada CBI includes approved business projects.
summary: Micro ecosystem; small-business finance comes from the Grenada Development Bank. A 2024 World Bank OECS project targets entrepreneurs in Grenada and Saint Lucia.
notes: OECS member, not an IDB borrowing member; regional support comes via CDB, Compete Caribbean, OECS and Caribbean Export. OECS Youth Empowerment Project small grants (US$5k) closed 2026-08-14. The GIDC (investment agency) website did not resolve in Oct 2026, so it is left out.

company_setup: Sociedad Anonima registered with the Registro Mercantil (online via MINECO); foreigners can own 100%; about 2-4 weeks.
summary: Largest Central American economy, with a growing scene in Guatemala City and Quetzaltenango. Impact investing (Pomona, Alterna), university programmes (UFM) and regional VCs drive it. It hosts a Startup World Cup round and the Volcano Innovation Summit.
notes: Startup World Cup Guatemala 2026 was held 2026-06-23. Invest Guatemala's domain now redirects elsewhere, so it is left out. AGEXPORT's site timed out.

company_setup: OHADA SARL/SAS via APIP one-stop shop (quick, low cost).
summary: Conakry hosts most of the country's startups; mining-sponsored programmes (Rio Tinto Future Champions) and Saboutech incubator; little VC.
notes: Transitional military government. Future Champions Hackathon 2026 (Rio Tinto/Ecobank/TotalEnergies) launched 2026-10-15; no official URL verified. Orange Fab Guinée exists but its site was unreachable.

company_setup: OHADA company via the Centro de Formalização de Empresas (one-stop shop). Diaspora founders typically incorporate in Portugal or elsewhere.
summary: Very nascent ecosystem; no dedicated accelerators or VCs verified; support comes mainly from pan-African and donor programmes.
notes: Political instability. No national startup agency website verified.

company_setup: Company under the Companies Act via the Deeds and Commercial Registries Authority; foreigners can own; about 1-3 weeks.
summary: Oil-boom economy with fast GDP growth but a tiny startup scene in Georgetown. Support is mostly SME loans and grants from the Small Business Bureau, plus Caribbean regional programmes.
notes: The GO-Invest (investment agency) site refused connections in Oct 2026, so it is left out. Local-content rules favour Guyanese-owned firms in oil and gas supply.

company_setup: SA (societe anonyme) registered with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; the CFI one-stop shop helps foreign investors. Many diaspora founders incorporate in the US and operate in Haiti.
summary: Fragile state with a severe security crisis. Startup activity is small, centred on Port-au-Prince and Cap-Haitien, and driven by diaspora events (Haiti Tech Summit), IDB Lab pilots and new youth labs such as AyitiLab (launched June 2026).
notes: As of Oct 2026, insecurity in Port-au-Prince severely limits operations. AyitiLab (Avenir Foundation, MCI, ESIH) launched 2026-06-29; no working official URL was found. IDB projects (Haiti Startup Talent, CARIBEquity ANGAJE) are in preparation. Diaspora and US incorporation are the main routes.

company_setup: Sociedad Anonima or S. de R.L. via the Chamber of Commerce one-stop shop; foreigners can own; about 2-4 weeks.
summary: Small ecosystem in Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula. The Founder Institute runs a virtual chapter and Davivienda brought Espaciotec here in 2026. SENPRENDE and BANHPROVI provide public support, and CABEI is headquartered in Tegucigalpa.
notes: The government's long-running Honduras StartUp seed programme (IHCIETI) has no current official page. The BCIE/KfW/EU DINAMICA II seed grants selected 50 Honduran firms in 2025.

startup_visa: Investment as Entrepreneurs (Immigration Department), plus the Top Talent Pass Scheme for high earners and graduates, https://www.immd.gov.hk/eng/services/visas/investment.html
company_setup: Private company limited by shares. Online incorporation with the Companies Registry, no residency requirement but a local company secretary and address are needed. Takes about 1-5 days and costs about HK$1,500-2,000 in fees. Profits tax is 8.25% on the first HK$2M.
summary: International finance hub with a startup scene focused on fintech, biotech, AI and Greater Bay Area access, anchored by HKSTP and Cyberport. Government funding has grown sharply through ITF, the HK Investment Corporation and talent schemes. SenseTime, Klook and WeLab are notable names.
notes: As of Oct 2026 the Technology Voucher Programme (TVP) is not listed on the ITF programme index and its old ITF page returns 404. Its current status could not be confirmed, so it is left out. hkstp.org timed out and cyberport.hk blocked automated fetches during research, so incubation funding amounts and intake dates were not confirmed.

company_setup: Kft. (LLC), HUF 3M minimum capital; e-registration through a lawyer typically within 1-2 business days; foreigners can incorporate remotely via attorney.
summary: Budapest-centred ecosystem with notable successes Prezi, LogMeIn, Ustream and Bitrise. State-backed Hiventures is the largest early-stage investor; private VCs include Day One and Portfolion.
notes: Few verifiable accelerators with open calls in Oct 2026. Hiventures ticket sizes not stated on site.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; non-EEA founders need a work/residence permit via the Directorate of Immigration)
company_setup: Private limited company (ehf.), minimum share capital ISK 500,000; registered with Iceland Revenue and Customs (Skatturinn) company register; EEA nationals can register with an Icelandic ID number.
summary: Small Reykjavik-based ecosystem strong in gaming (CCP), fintech (Meniga), health (Kerecis, sold to Coloplast), ocean and climate tech (Carbfix). Public funding via Rannis Technology Development Fund and the Kria innovation fund.
notes: Nyskopunarmidstod Islands (Innovation Center Iceland) has been dissolved. Rannis grant amounts not shown on the island.is page.

startup_visa: No dedicated startup visa; foreign founders use the e-Business/Business visa (multi-year, multiple entry) or Employment visa. DPIIT recognition is available to Indian-incorporated entities with foreign founders.
company_setup: Private Limited Company via MCA SPICe+ online form; 100% FDI under automatic route in most sectors; needs at least one resident director and Indian registered office; DSC can be obtained remotely; typically 1-3 weeks and under US$500 in government fees.
summary: World's third-largest startup ecosystem with 150k+ DPIIT-recognised startups and 100+ unicorns; hubs in Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai. Strong in SaaS, fintech, consumer internet and deeptech; notable IPOs include Zomato (Eternal), Swiggy and Ola Electric.
notes: As of 2026-10-20. Karnataka ELEVATE NxT deadline from secondary sources (aggregators); confirm on the state portal. startup.karnataka.gov.in did not resolve, so the dept site is used. BIRAC BIG 26th call not yet announced. Web-search quota ran out mid-research, so several deadlines are pattern-based.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; investor KITAS and Golden Visa via Immigration), https://evisa.imigrasi.go.id/
company_setup: Foreign-owned companies must be a PT PMA, with an investment plan over IDR 10bn per business line; the minimum paid-up capital was cut to IDR 2.5bn in 2025. Licensing is done online through OSS. A local PT is cheaper but needs Indonesian shareholders, so many founders use a Singapore holding company.
summary: Largest startup market in Southeast Asia, centred on Jakarta, with unicorns such as GoTo, Traveloka, Bukalapak and Xendit. Active local VCs and corporate VCs from state banks and telcos; funding cooled after 2022 but early-stage activity continues.
notes: Komdigi replaced Kominfo in late 2024. 1000 Startup Digital and the ANGIN site could not be confirmed online in Oct 2026 and are omitted. Few published accelerator deadlines found.

company_setup: Private joint-stock or LLC via Iran's companies registration office; foreign founders face severe sanctions and banking barriers.
summary: Large, isolated domestic tech market (Tehran) with local champions like Digikala, Snapp and Cafe Bazaar, supported by the knowledge-based company law and state innovation funds.
notes: Sanctions: comprehensive US sanctions and UN sanctions re-imposed via snapback (Sep 2025); EU measures; June 2025 Israel-Iran war. International VC and payments effectively unavailable; Iranian government sites geo-block foreign traffic, so URLs confirmed only by DNS/403 response.

company_setup: LLC registration with the Companies Registrar (Baghdad) or KRG; foreigners usually need a local partner or investment licence; several weeks.
summary: Fast-growing but early ecosystem in Baghdad, Erbil and Basra, driven by a young population, fintech and delivery apps; heavily cash-based economy.
notes: Security and political risk; Iraqi Development Fund status not verified and omitted.

startup_visa: Start-up Entrepreneur Programme (STEP): innovative high-potential startup with about €50,000 funding, evaluated with Enterprise Ireland, https://www.irishimmigration.ie/coming-to-work-in-ireland/what-are-my-options-for-working-in-ireland/coming-to-work-for-more-than-90-days/start-up-entrepreneur-programme-step/
company_setup: Private company limited by shares (LTD) registered with the Companies Registration Office (CORE online, about €50–100, around 5 working days). Needs an EEA-resident director or a non-resident director bond. 12.5% trading corporation tax.
summary: Compact, well-supported ecosystem centred on Dublin with hubs in Cork, Galway and Limerick, boosted by EU HQs of Google, Meta and others. Enterprise Ireland is a hands-on co-investor; notable companies include Stripe (Irish founders), Intercom, Fenergo and Wayflyer.
notes: The Competitive Start Fund no longer appears on Enterprise Ireland's site; the Pre-Seed Start Fund has taken its place. The NDRC Accelerator says rolling intake but applications are currently closed. The €50k STEP threshold is from prior guidance, because the immigration page content could not be read. Web search budget ran out mid-batch, so some deadlines are 'unknown'.

startup_visa: Innovation Visa for Foreign Technology Entrepreneurs (B/2 up to 24 months via IIA landing-pad incubators, then expert visa), https://innovationisrael.org.il/en/programs/tech-innovation-visa/
company_setup: Ltd (private company) registered with the Israeli Corporations Authority; can be done remotely via a local lawyer, typically 1-2 weeks and a few thousand US$ in fees. Many founders use a Delaware C-corp with an Israeli subsidiary.
summary: One of the world's densest startup ecosystems, centred on Tel Aviv, Jerusalem and Haifa; strong in cyber, AI, semiconductors, fintech and defence tech. Major exits include Wiz (Google), Mobileye and Waze.
notes: IIA site blocks automated access; amounts from its English pages may differ from current Hebrew calls. Regional war since Oct 2023 has affected operations and some VC flows; check Hebrew portal for open calls.

startup_visa: Italia Startup Visa (MIMIT fast-track for non-EU founders of innovative startups); official portal was unreachable during verification
company_setup: SRL (from €1 capital; simplified SRLS) via notary; innovative startups register in the special section of the Companies Register (startup.registroimprese.it); 1–3 weeks.
summary: Mid-sized ecosystem led by Milan, with Turin, Rome and Bologna as secondary hubs; public capital via CDP Venture Capital (National Innovation Fund) and the innovative-startup regime. Strengths in fintech, deep tech, food and industrial tech; notable companies include Satispay, Scalapay and Bending Spoons.
notes: MIMIT and Italia Startup Visa portals were unreachable during checks. LUISS EnLabs and LVenture now operate as Zest. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

company_setup: Private company limited by shares, registered online with the Companies Office of Jamaica (BizRegistration); foreigners can own 100%. Usually a few days.
summary: Largest English-speaking Caribbean ecosystem, centred on Kingston. Support comes from DBJ's BIGEE programme, UTech's Technology Innovation Centre, the Caribbean Climate Innovation Centre and the FirstAngels Caribbean network. Junior Market listings on the JSE give SMEs a capital route.
notes: BIGEE's IDB-backed IGNITE/IGF grants paused when the disbursement window ended in March 2025. J$900M+ budgeted for BIGEE in FY2026/27, incl. a planned SME VC fund (not yet launched as of Oct 2026). In March 2026 UTech TIC, RevUP and FirstAngels signed a 3-year pipeline MOU.

startup_visa: Startup Visa (Designated Activities No.44) through certified local governments such as Tokyo: one year, extendable to about two years, then a switch to Business Manager, which since Oct 2025 needs JPY 30M capital and one full-time staff member. https://www.investtokyo.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/jp/oursupports/bdc-tokyo/startupvisa.html
company_setup: Kabushiki Kaisha (KK) or Godo Kaisha (GK). A foreigner can incorporate through a judicial scrivener without being resident, but a Japanese bank account and address are practical hurdles. Takes about 2-4 weeks. The Tokyo One-Stop Center helps with filings.
summary: Asia's second-largest ecosystem by VC volume, centred on Tokyo, with Osaka, Kyoto and Fukuoka as secondary hubs. Strong deep tech, B2B SaaS and university spin-outs, backed by the government's 5-Year Startup Development Plan. Most exits are IPOs on TSE Growth, and M&A is rising.
notes: In Oct 2026 the JETRO website showed a suspension notice after unauthorized access, so some JETRO links may be intermittent. The Business Manager visa capital requirement rose to JPY 30M in Oct 2025, according to the Tokyo startup visa page. For GX_UPP the submission window is 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-17. Web search was exhausted during research, so several entries were verified by site checks only.

startup_visa: none (investor residency via Ministry of Investment; no dedicated startup visa verified)
company_setup: LLC or Private Shareholding Company registered with the Companies Control Department; foreigners can own most tech businesses; about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Amman-centred ecosystem with strong software, gaming and e-commerce talent; exits include Maktoob (Yahoo) and Jamalon. The World Bank-backed ISSF fund of funds anchors local VC.
notes: Flat6Labs Amman's last published deadline was Feb 2025. Regional conflict has dampened 2024-26 funding.

startup_visa: No standalone startup visa. Astana Hub participants get a simplified visa and labour regime, and Astana Hub runs a Digital Nomad Visa / Residency for IT specialists, https://astanahub.com/l/digital-nomad
company_setup: LLP (TOO) registered online via egov.kz in 1-3 days. Foreigners usually incorporate in person or through a representative. AIFC (Astana) offers a common-law jurisdiction for funds and fintech. Astana Hub participants get 0% CIT/VAT on qualifying IT income.
summary: Central Asia's largest startup ecosystem, centred on Astana Hub (Astana) and Almaty. About US$209m raised by Kazakh IT startups in 2025, dominated by AI. Notable successes include Kaspi.kz and Higgsfield AI.
notes: Oct 2026: no Astana Hub accelerator calls were open; check astanahub.com for new ones. Alem Ventures, a US$1bn-target fund of funds (first close US$115m, Oct 2025), was left out because no official site was found. Tech Garden (techgarden.kz) and Terricon Valley were left out because their sites were down or placeholders. MOST Ventures (most.vc) was left out because the domain is parked.

startup_visa: none (Kenya Startup Bill pending; founders typically use Class G investor work permit), https://immigration.go.ke/
company_setup: Private limited company registered online via eCitizen Business Registration Service; foreigners can incorporate, usually within days.
summary: One of Africa's big four ecosystems, centred on Nairobi ('Silicon Savannah'); strong in fintech (M-Pesa), climate, agritech and logistics. Hubs include iHub, Nailab and Konza Technopolis.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Search quota ran out mid-research, so deadlines come from programme pages; many show no published date. Savannah Fund, Chui Ventures and Enza Capital domains looked parked, and Nailab's site showed a hosting placeholder, so all four were left out.

company_setup: Business names and companies registered with the Ministry of Tourism, Commerce, Industry and Cooperatives (MTCIC), which also registers foreign investment.
summary: Micro-economy in South Tarawa dependent on fisheries licences and aid, with very limited private-sector startup activity.
notes: No accelerators or VCs exist locally. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

company_setup: SH.P.K. (LLC) registered with the Kosovo Business Registration Agency (ARBK); foreigners can own 100%; registration is fast and low cost.
summary: Youngest population in Europe and a strong IT outsourcing base around Pristina and Prizren, supported by the ICT association STIKK and donor-backed hubs. Euro-based; public support comes via the Ministry of Industry, Entrepreneurship, Trade and Innovation (MINTI) and KIESA.
notes: Innovation Centre Kosovo (ickk.org) refused connections and Zephyr Angels had a certificate error, so both were excluded. Kosovo is Horizon Europe associated, but some international platforms do not list it as a country.

company_setup: WLL via Ministry of Commerce; 100% foreign ownership possible via KDIPA licence; several weeks.
summary: Small but wealthy market; notable startups include Talabat and Carriage (both acquired). Government National Fund for SMEs and family offices are main funders.
notes: Brilliant Lab domain no longer active; omitted.

startup_visa: none (visa-free for 60+ countries; investor residence from US$100k via invest.gov.kg)
company_setup: LLC can be registered fully remotely in about 3 business days with 100% foreign ownership. HTP residents pay 0% CIT/VAT/sales tax, a 1% fee to HTP and 5% PIT.
summary: Small but active IT-export scene in Bishkek built around the High Technology Park's 0% tax regime. Outsourcing and dev shops (e.g. Mad Devs) dominate.
notes: Oct 2026: no local VC fund could be verified because web search hit its limit. Accelerate Prosperity KG terms couldn't be fetched (site blocked bots).

company_setup: Enterprise registration with the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, with foreign investment approvals via the Investment Promotion Department; usually takes several weeks. Many founders use a Thai or Singapore entity for fundraising.
summary: Very early-stage ecosystem in Vientiane, supported by donors (KOICA, World Bank, DFAT) and the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, which hosted the first National Startup Fest in April 2026. The MSME and Startup Innovation Center (MSIC) is being developed with KOICA.
notes: Lao SME Promotion Fund and MSMEPA sites could not be resolved in Oct 2026. TOHLAO activity since 2025 not confirmed, so it is omitted.

startup_visa: Latvian startup residence permit under the Startup Law (via Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs), https://www.pmlp.gov.lv/en
company_setup: SIA (limited liability), registered with the Register of Enterprises, online with eID; e-residents of Latvia or Estonia can sign electronically; low minimum capital.
summary: Riga-based ecosystem with startups such as Printful, Sonarworks and airBaltic-adjacent aerospace/drone firms; supportive Startup Law with tax benefits. Funding via ALTUM-backed VC funds and LIAA programs.
notes: LIAA English pages give few startup program details; amounts for ALTUM VC funds not published on overview page.

company_setup: SAL or SARL via notary and commercial register; capital controls make local banking hard, so many founders incorporate abroad (UAE, Delaware) and keep a Lebanese subsidiary.
summary: Beirut historically had a vibrant scene (Anghami listed on Nasdaq) but the 2019 banking collapse, 2020 port blast and 2024 war hit it hard; many startups now operate from the Gulf or Europe.
notes: Financial crisis since 2019 (BDL Circular 331 VC scheme is effectively defunct). Funding is scarce; status of Flat6Labs Beirut unclear and omitted.

company_setup: Private company via One Stop Business Facilitation Centre (online); foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Tiny Maseru-based ecosystem; BEDCO incubation and LNDC investment promotion are the main supports.

company_setup: Company registration at the Liberia Business Registry (one-stop shop); NIC supports investors.
summary: Very small Monrovia ecosystem with iLab Liberia and Orange Digital Center; donor-funded SME support dominates.
notes: Few verifiable startup-specific programmes.

company_setup: Registration via Ministry of Economy; split governance and banking issues; diaspora entities (Tunisia, Malta, UAE) are common.
summary: Very early ecosystem in Tripoli and Benghazi, supported mainly by NGOs and donors; e-payments and delivery apps are emerging.
notes: Political division and periodic conflict; UN arms embargo and asset freezes on some entities. No verified active VCs.

startup_visa: none (EEA/Swiss nationals face residence quotas; no startup visa)
company_setup: AG or GmbH registered with the Office of Justice commercial register; local director/qualified person usually required; formation typically via a fiduciary.
summary: Tiny, wealthy EEA microstate with a finance, fintech/blockchain (TVTG Blockchain Act) and precision-manufacturing base (Hilti, Ivoclar). Very few local startup programs; founders rely on the Technopark, University of Liechtenstein and Swiss/Austrian networks.
notes: Liechtenstein is EEA but not associated to Horizon Europe, so EIC Accelerator eligibility is doubtful; no local VC funds verified.

startup_visa: Lithuania Startup Visa (Startup Lithuania expert committee; 2-year TRP extendable to 5), https://startupvisalithuania.com/
company_setup: UAB (private limited) registered at the Centre of Registers, online with e-signature (Lithuanian, Estonian/Latvian eID accepted); low minimum capital; a few days.
summary: Vilnius and Kaunas ecosystem with unicorns Vinted and Nord Security; strong fintech licensing hub (Bank of Lithuania), gaming and laser/biotech. Startup Lithuania (Innovation Agency) runs the startup visa.
notes: INVEGA now redirects to ILTE (National Development Bank). ILTE site blocks automated fetch; instruments not itemised.

startup_visa: none (non-EU founders apply for a self-employed residence permit)
company_setup: SARL (€12k capital, notarised) or simplified SARL-S (from €1); business permit from the Ministry of the Economy; guidance via Guichet.lu; about 2–4 weeks.
summary: Small but well-funded ecosystem in Luxembourg City, built on its financial centre and EU institutions. Strengths in fintech, space resources, cybersecurity and fund tech; government support via Luxinnovation and Fit 4 Start.
notes: Fit 4 Start #17 cohort has been selected; next call date not found. LHoFT Catapult 2026 editions (Green Fintech, FundTech, Kickstarter) all listed as closed. Luxembourg Future Fund site not reachable, so left out. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

startup_visa: none (no startup visa; non-residents typically enter via investment or talent schemes)
company_setup: Sociedade por quotas (limited company), minimum capital MOP25,000. Registered through the Commercial and Movable Property Registry, with help from IPIM's Investor One Stop Service. Takes about 1-3 weeks.
summary: Small, government-led ecosystem built around youth entrepreneurship, diversification beyond gaming, and the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin. Support is mostly interest-free loans, incubation space and Greater Bay Area programs.
notes: No Macau-based VC with a verifiable official site was found. Founders usually raise from Hong Kong or Mainland funds. Many Hengqin youth-entrepreneurship programs are listed on Mainland sites that could not be verified.

startup_visa: none; investor visas via EDBM, https://www.edbm.mg/
company_setup: SARL via EDBM one-stop shop; foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Antananarivo ecosystem, French-speaking, with BPO, agri and fintech activity; Miarakap is the main local impact investor and accelerator.

startup_visa: none; business residence permits via MITC, https://mitc.mw/
company_setup: Private company via the Registrar General online registry; foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Small Lilongwe/Blantyre ecosystem focused on agritech, fintech and energy; supported mainly by donors and impact investors.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. mHub and NEEF domains did not resolve and were left out.

startup_visa: Malaysia Tech Entrepreneur Programme (MTEP, MDEC): 1-year pass for new founders, 5-year for established entrepreneurs/investors, https://www.mdec.my/programmes/mtep
company_setup: Sdn Bhd registered with SSM online (MyCoID), around RM1,000 in fees and a few days; at least one resident director is required, and foreign-owned firms face higher paid-up capital rules for some licences.
summary: Kuala Lumpur and Penang host a growing ecosystem led by MDEC, Cradle and MRANTI, with notable companies such as Grab (founded in Malaysia), Carsome, Aerodyne and Funding Societies Malaysia. Strong government grant and fund-of-funds support, with equity crowdfunding regulated by the Securities Commission.
notes: MaGIC and Technology Park Malaysia were merged into MRANTI in 2022, and mymagic.my is offline. MAVCAP's old domain now redirects elsewhere, so it is omitted. Cradle had published no CIP call dates as of Oct 2026.

company_setup: Register a private company online via the Ministry business portal; foreign investment needs approval via Invest Maldives and is restricted in some sectors.
summary: Tiny Malé-centred ecosystem dominated by tourism; digital startups are few, supported mainly by SME finance and government business registration.
notes: As of 2026-10-20. No accelerators or VCs found. Diaspora/remote route: incorporate abroad (Delaware or Estonia e-Residency).

company_setup: OHADA SARL/SAS via API-Mali one-stop shop. Diaspora route: incorporate abroad with local subsidiary.
summary: Bamako ecosystem with Donilab, Orange Digital Center and Orange Corners; young population, agritech/fintech/edtech focus; capital very limited.
notes: Military government; left ECOWAS (AES) in Jan 2025; security and sanctions risk. APEJ loan range from a secondary guide. Donilab and API-Mali sites unreachable.

startup_visa: Malta Startup Residence Programme (Malta Enterprise endorsement, residence via Identita)
company_setup: Private limited company (Ltd) via the Malta Business Registry, minimum share capital EUR 1,165 (20% paid up); online filing possible through a registered agent; about a week.
summary: Small EU island ecosystem strong in iGaming, fintech and blockchain regulation, with Malta Enterprise offering generous startup grants and repayable advances. English-speaking, Valletta-centred.
notes: Startup Residence Programme page URL not confirmed (old path 404). Takeoff site shows injected casino spam in menus; content otherwise current.

company_setup: Domestic corporations registered with the RMI Registrar of Corporations; foreign investors need a Foreign Investment Business License. A non-resident corporate registry is also available.
summary: Small US-dollar economy in Majuro under a Compact of Free Association with the US. Business support comes through the US-funded Pacific SBDC network.
notes: No local accelerators or VCs exist. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

company_setup: SARL via the one-stop guichet unique of APIM; low capital requirement; diaspora entities common.
summary: Very small digital ecosystem in Nouakchott; growth tied to mobile money and gas projects. Support mainly from donors.
notes: No verified local accelerators or VCs; regional funds (Partech Africa, Seedstars) rarely invest here.

startup_visa: Residency by Innovation (Occupation Permit route for innovative startups), https://residency.mu/invest/residency-by-innovation/
company_setup: Private company via CBRD online registration in days; widely used by foreigners as a pan-African holding jurisdiction (Global Business Licence).
summary: Ebene-centred hub for fintech, offshore structuring and pan-African holding companies; government MRIC grants, EDB promotion and the Turbine incubator support startups.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. MRIC scheme pages give no amounts or deadlines. Turbine's page shows a '300K Cash Reward' without naming the currency.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; founders use temporary resident visas via INM, https://www.gob.mx/inm)
company_setup: Typical entity S.A.P.I. de C.V. or S.A.S.; foreigners can incorporate but need an RFC (tax ID), notary and usually a local legal representative; about 2–6 weeks and US$1–3k. Many VC-backed startups use a Delaware or Cayman holdco.
summary: Second-largest LatAm ecosystem, centred on Mexico City, Monterrey and Guadalajara; strong in fintech and e-commerce. Unicorns include Kavak, Clip, Bitso and Konfío.
notes: As of Oct 2026 there is no federal startup grant program (INADEM was closed in 2019); support is mainly state level and via SECIHTI calls. allvp.vc redirects to hi.vc; relationship unconfirmed. Wayra no longer lists Mexico among its hubs. Check sizes mostly unpublished.

company_setup: Companies registered with the FSM Registrar of Corporations; foreign investment permits are issued nationally and by the states.
summary: Small US-dollar economy across four states (Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae) under a Compact of Free Association with the US. Business support comes through SBDC centres and the FSM Development Bank.
notes: No local accelerators or VCs exist. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

startup_visa: none (Moldova IT Park IT Visa for foreign IT specialists, https://mitp.md/why-mitp/it-visa/)
company_setup: SRL (LLC) registered with the Public Services Agency, usually within a day; foreigners can own 100%; tech firms can join Moldova IT Park for a 7% single tax on turnover.
summary: Fast-growing small ecosystem in Chisinau with 300+ startups that raised about US$17M in 2025, anchored by the Moldova IT Park 7% single-tax regime, Tekwill and the Startup Moldova foundation. EU candidate status opens EU programmes; local VC is still thin.
notes: ODA monthly windows close early when the budget is spent. ODA Fund of Funds (first-loss tranche, MDL 180M) has no selected managers yet as of Oct 2026. Mozaic angel community (EUR 25-100k tickets) and Business Angels Moldova exist but their websites could not be verified (DNS/certificate errors), so they were left out.

startup_visa: none (residence via Monaco residency card; MonacoTech requires creating a Monaco company within 18 months)
company_setup: SARL or SAM; requires prior government authorisation (Direction du Developpement Economique); local office lease needed; slow and costly versus EU.
summary: Small government-backed ecosystem built around MonacoTech (incubator) and Monaco Boost, with focus on green/blue tech, yachting, medtech and AI; capital comes mainly from family offices and HNWIs.
notes: Monaco is outside the EU and Horizon Europe association; EIC not applicable. Monaco Angels domain appears parked, excluded.

company_setup: LLC registered with the General Authority for State Registration. Foreign-invested companies generally need foreign equity of at least about US$100k to register as such, so smaller foreign founders often use local partners. Takes about 2-4 weeks.
summary: Small ecosystem centred on Ulaanbaatar, strongest in fintech, e-commerce and govtech (e-Mongolia). The Mongolian Startup Association runs community events, and the first local VC funds are only forming. Capital mostly comes from banks, conglomerates and development finance institutions.
notes: No Mongolia-based VC or accelerator with a current, verifiable official site was confirmed. The Mongolian Startup Association site mentions the first local VC fund forming in 2025. The SME Agency site lists loan intake but no published terms.

company_setup: DOO (LLC) registered with the Central Register of Business Entities (CRPS); foreigners may own 100%, usually in person or via power of attorney; registration takes a few days at low cost.
summary: Small ecosystem centred on Podgorica and Niksic, driven mainly by the public Innovation Fund of Montenegro (Fond za inovacije) and the Tehnopolis innovation centre. Euro-based economy; few local investors, so most startups rely on grants, regional VCs and EU programmes.
notes: Innovation Fund runs annual cycles; most 2026 calls opened in May and closed in June. As of 2026-10-20 only the POC call is open. No Montenegrin VC fund verified; Science and Technology Park site could not be verified.

company_setup: SARL via CRI online platform; 100% foreign ownership allowed; about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Casablanca and Rabat-led ecosystem with strong state push (Digital Morocco 2030, Innov Invest Fund, UM6P); strengths in fintech, agritech and outsourcing.
notes: World Bank rated Innov Invest Fund I 'Highly Satisfactory' (Sep 2026); FII 2 selecting up to 20 support structures.

company_setup: Lda via the Balcao de Atendimento Unico (one-stop shop); foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Maputo-based ecosystem, Portuguese-speaking, with mobile money (M-Pesa) and donor-backed incubation; gas sector drives investment.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

company_setup: Private company registered online via MyCO (DICA), which is technically quick, but banking, sanctions and conflict risks make it impractical for most founders. Diaspora founders usually incorporate in Singapore or Thailand.
summary: Ecosystem contracted sharply after the February 2021 military coup; many investors and accelerators stopped work. Some social-enterprise support continues in Yangon, but most international capital is unavailable.
notes: Post-coup conflict and sanctions since 2021: international VC is effectively unavailable. Phandeeyar's site could not be resolved in Oct 2026, so it is omitted.

startup_visa: none; investor permits via NIPDB, https://www.nipdb.com/
company_setup: Private company or close corporation via BIPA online registration; foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Small Windhoek-based ecosystem; NUST's Namibia Business Innovation Institute, NCRST funding and the Development Bank of Namibia support early ventures; green hydrogen is driving new investment.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. The NUST Namibia Business Innovation Institute site returned an empty page and was left out.

company_setup: Companies registered under Nauru's business registration law with government; contact the Nauru Chamber of Commerce for guidance.
summary: Micro-economy with a very small private sector and no formal startup ecosystem.
notes: The Nauru government website could not be reached, so no national SME agency URL could be verified. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.
