company_setup: Private limited company via Office of Company Registrar online; foreign investment needs Department of Industry or IBN approval and a minimum FDI threshold (NPR 20 million as of 2024); repatriation regulated by Nepal Rastra Bank.
summary: Kathmandu-based nascent ecosystem; fintech, e-commerce and IT outsourcing. Government introduced concessional startup loans and the Startup Enterprise program.
notes: As of 2026-10-20. No local VC or accelerator site could be verified (Zerohub, NEST, True Venture links failed). Diaspora route: incorporate abroad (e.g. Delaware via Stripe Atlas) given FDI thresholds.

startup_visa: Start-up residence permit (1 year, requires an RVO-approved facilitator), https://ind.nl/en/residence-permits/work/start-up
company_setup: BV with €0.01 minimum capital via notarial deed and KVK registration; can be done remotely via notary with power of attorney; around 1 week.
summary: Dense, internationally oriented ecosystem around Amsterdam, Delft, Eindhoven and Utrecht. Strengths in fintech, deep tech (photonics, semiconductors), agrifood and health; notable companies include Adyen, Mollie, Bunq and Booking.com.
notes: WBSO 2027 changes announced 15 Sep 2026; Invest-NL site was not reachable from our checker (connection error) but is the known official domain. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

startup_visa: none (Entrepreneur Work Visa closed to new applications); Business Investor Work Visa requires NZ$1m+ in an established business, https://www.immigration.govt.nz/visas/business-investor-work-visa/
company_setup: Limited company registered online with the NZ Companies Office in about a day (about NZ$150). Needs at least one director living in NZ, or in Australia and also a director of an Australian company.
summary: Compact but internationally connected ecosystem centred on Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch, strong in SaaS, agritech, climate, fintech, space and deep tech. Notable outcomes include Xero, Rocket Lab, Vend and LanzaTech roots.
notes: As of 2026-10-20: Callaghan Innovation is being disestablished. Its grants (New to R&D, Career, Experience), RDTI and founder support now sit with MBIE Innovation Services. Callaghan's Technology Incubator Programme stays with Callaghan pending legislation to move it to a Public Research Organisation, so it is left out. The Ārohia Trailblazer and Evidence grants closed in Dec 2025. The Entrepreneur Work Visa is closed to new applicants. The Icehouse (business growth) website blocked verification, so only Icehouse Ventures is listed. Return On Science is a programme backed by UniServices and MBIE. Fintech Lab's 22 November deadline has no year on the page and is read as 2026. Exchange rate used: NZ$1 = about US$0.58.

company_setup: Sociedad Anonima registered via the Ventanilla Unica de Inversiones and Registro Mercantil; foreigners can own; about 2-4 weeks.
summary: Very limited startup activity under an authoritarian political climate. Impact Hub Managua and university incubators (UNAN) are among the few actors. Mostly small-business fairs.
notes: As of Oct 2026, mass closure of NGOs and universities, plus US/EU sanctions on officials, deter foreign investors and donors. Regional VCs such as Carao say they cover all Spanish-speaking LatAm, but no Nicaraguan deals were verified.

company_setup: OHADA SARL/SAS via Maison de l'Entreprise one-stop shop. Diaspora route: incorporate abroad.
summary: Very nascent Niamey ecosystem (CIPMEN incubator historically); agri financing via FISAN; capital extremely scarce.
notes: Military government since 2023; left ECOWAS (AES) Jan 2025; donor programmes partly suspended. CIPMEN site unreachable; omitted.

company_setup: Private limited company (Ltd) registered online with the Corporate Affairs Commission (about 1-2 weeks); foreign-owned firms also register with NIPC and must meet minimum share-capital rules. Itana digital free zone (Lagos) offers remote incorporation.
summary: Africa's largest startup ecosystem by deal count, centred on Lagos with Abuja secondary; strengths in fintech (Flutterwave, Moniepoint, Paystack exit to Stripe), logistics and creative tech.
notes: Startup Act 2022 seed-fund disbursement status unconfirmed as of Oct 2026. Several hub/fund sites (e.g. Lagos Innovates, DBN short domain) were unreachable and omitted.

company_setup: Not possible for foreign founders under current sanctions. Private enterprise is not legally recognised.
summary: No accessible private startup ecosystem. The economy is state-controlled and under comprehensive UN, US and EU sanctions, so foreign investment, payments and tech transfer are effectively prohibited.
notes: Sanctions as of Oct 2026: any investment or business is effectively prohibited. Listed for completeness only.

company_setup: DOOEL/DOO (LLC) via Central Registry of North Macedonia, one-stop registration typically within days; foreigners can own 100%.
summary: Small but active ecosystem concentrated in Skopje, with outsourcing-heavy IT sector and growing startup scene. Main public funder is the Fund for Innovation and Technology Development (FITD), backed by the World Bank; regional VC South Central Ventures has a local presence.
notes: FITD website (fitr.mk) is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read; latest confirmed FITD startup call was 2024, so 2025-2026 calls are unverified. BAU Accelerator site had an expired certificate and was excluded.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; self-employed residence permit via UDI), https://www.udi.no/en/want-to-apply/work-immigration/self-employed/
company_setup: Aksjeselskap (AS), minimum share capital NOK 30,000; registered via Altinn with the Bronnoysund Register Centre; online filing needs Norwegian e-ID.
summary: Oslo-led ecosystem with Bergen and Trondheim (NTNU); strengths in ocean, energy, climate tech, fintech and seafood tech. Strong public funding via Innovation Norway, Research Council and SkatteFUNN; notable exits include Kahoot! and Cognite growth.
notes: Innovation Norway phase grant amounts not stated on English pages; check raskavklaring.innovasjonnorge.no for personalised offers.

company_setup: LLC via Invest Easy portal; 100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors; 1-2 weeks.
summary: Muscat-centred ecosystem backed by state funds (Oman Technology Fund, Future Fund Oman) and the SME Development Authority; focus on logistics, energy and tourism tech.

startup_visa: none (business visa via Board of Investment; no dedicated startup visa)
company_setup: Private limited company via SECP eServices online, typically 1-3 days and low fees; foreigners can own 100% in most sectors but foreign directors/shareholders need security clearance.
summary: Growing ecosystem centred on Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad; fintech, e-commerce and logistics lead. Funding fell sharply after the 2022 peak; Ignite runs a national network of incubation centres.
notes: As of 2026-10-20. NIC deadlines not published; cohorts recruit on rolling basis. LUMS NEST and Indus Valley Capital sites did not resolve during checks and were left out.

company_setup: Companies registered with the Registrar of Corporations. Foreign-owned businesses need Foreign Investment Board approval.
summary: Small, tourism-driven US-dollar economy in Koror under a Compact of Free Association with the US. Business support comes through the Palau SBDC.
notes: The domain palauchamber.com no longer belongs to the chamber, so the PIPSO listing is used instead. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

company_setup: Companies register with the Ministry of National Economy; movement and banking constraints lead many founders to incorporate in Jordan, UAE or Delaware.
summary: Small tech scene in Ramallah, Nablus and (formerly) Gaza, focused on outsourcing and software; severely disrupted by the Gaza war since Oct 2023 and West Bank restrictions.
notes: War in Gaza since Oct 2023 has destroyed much infrastructure; Gaza Sky Geeks operates largely remotely/online. Ibtikar Fund II raised a US$15M first close.

startup_visa: none (Remote worker short-stay visa and Friendly Nations residency via Migracion: https://www.migracion.gob.pa)
company_setup: Sociedad Anonima or SRL via a Panamanian lawyer (registered agent) at the Registro Publico; can be done remotely; about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Regional logistics and finance hub. Ciudad del Saber (City of Knowledge) is the main incubator and accelerator, with 150+ firms incubated. SENACYT funds innovation, and regional VCs (Carao, Magma, NXTP) invest. Fintech and logistics lead.
notes: AMPYME marked Capital Semilla 'inactive' (Oct 2026). SENACYT call listings load dynamically and could not be read. Venture Club Panama (angel pitch days) exists but its official URL was not verified.

company_setup: Company registered online with the Investment Promotion Authority (IPA). Foreign enterprises also need IPA foreign enterprise certification, which takes a few weeks.
summary: Small but growing digital and SME scene in Port Moresby and Lae, focused on mobile money, agri-business and services, supported by government SME and digital policy and by ADB and Australian aid.
notes: SME Corporation lists a Business Incubation Centre, a Women Enterprise Development Center and an SME Development Fund, but their current status is not published. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

company_setup: S.A. or SRL; EAS (Empresa por Acciones Simplificada) can be registered online quickly; foreigners can own 100%; low territorial tax regime.
summary: Small but active ecosystem in Asuncion. Public programmes include MITIC's InnovandoPY seed capital, CONACYT's PROINNOVA and incubators (INCUNA, PTI, Koga). Corporate programmes such as ueno/itti Moonshot are growing, and Paraguay Tech Week links founders to regional funds.
notes: InnovandoPY 9th edition awarded 7 startups US$20k each (July 2026). No Founder Institute Paraguay programme found for 2026.

startup_visa: none (no startup visa; ProInnóvate StartUp Perú PLUG offers seed for foreign startups landing in Peru; residence via Migraciones, https://www.gob.pe/migraciones)
company_setup: Typical entity S.A.C. or S.R.L.; foreigners can incorporate via notary with a RUC from SUNAT; about 1–3 weeks and US$300–800.
summary: Emerging ecosystem centred on Lima with fintech and B2B SaaS leaders (e.g. Yape, Culqi, Crehana, Kambista). Public seed funding through ProInnóvate's StartUp Perú anchors early-stage activity.
notes: gob.pe blocked automated fetching, so StartUp Perú dates come from news reports (13G closed Jan 2026; PLUG 2G for foreign startups announced Aug 2026). UTEC Ventures and Salkantaventures sites unreachable, so omitted. Local VC firms not verified. ~PEN 3.75/US$.

startup_visa: none confirmed (Innovative Startup Act provides for a startup visa, but no dedicated programme page verified)
company_setup: Domestic or foreign stock corporation registered with the SEC (eSPARC online), plus BIR and LGU permits; foreign ownership limits apply in some sectors. Takes about 2–4 weeks.
summary: Manila-centred ecosystem with fintech leaders (GCash/Mynt, Maya, PayMongo) and a legal framework under the Innovative Startup Act (RA 11337). Government grants via DOST, DTI and DICT; corporate VCs from Globe, Ayala, JG Summit and UnionBank.
notes: IdeaSpace site had certificate errors during verification and is omitted. PCIEERD SGF amount is as reported; check the current call.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; founders use standard business residence permits)
company_setup: sp. z o.o. (LLC), min capital PLN 5,000; online S24 registration in about a day (needs Polish e-ID/PESEL), otherwise via notary in 1-2 weeks. Non-residents can incorporate.
summary: Largest CEE startup market, centred on Warsaw, Krakow and Wroclaw, with deep software and deeptech talent. Public money via PFR Ventures fund-of-funds and PARP/NCBR grants dominates early-stage capital; notable exits include Booksy, DocPlanner and ElevenLabs roots.
notes: PARP and PFR Ventures sites block automated access; program names confirmed but current PARP call dates not verified (Oct 2026). EIC next full-proposal cut-off 2026-11-04.

startup_visa: Startup Visa (IAPMEI; requires contract with a certified incubator), https://startupportugal.com/programs/startup-visa/
company_setup: Lda with €1 minimum capital; 'Empresa na Hora' same-day formation; NIF required for foreigners; info on gov.pt.
summary: Growing ecosystem around Lisbon (Unicorn Factory Lisboa, Web Summit) and Porto, attracting international founders with visas and lower costs. Strengths in SaaS, fintech and AI; notable companies include Feedzai, OutSystems, Talkdesk and Sword Health.
notes: Startup Lisboa website has expired (Squarespace), so it is excluded. PRR startup voucher calls are closed. Lince Capital site unreachable during checks. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

startup_visa: none dedicated; Startup Qatar portal facilitates residency for founders, https://startupqatar.qa/en
company_setup: LLC via Ministry of Commerce or free-zone entity (QFC, QSTP, Qatar Free Zones); 100% foreign ownership in many sectors; 2-4 weeks.
summary: State-driven ecosystem around QSTP, Qatar Development Bank and the QIA US$1B fund-of-funds program; growing in fintech, sportstech and AI. Startup Qatar (Invest Qatar) is the one-stop portal.
notes: QSTP and QDB sites block automated access; XLR8 2026 dates not published.

company_setup: OHADA company via the Agence pour la Création des Entreprises (ACPCE) one-stop shop.
summary: Small Brazzaville/Pointe-Noire ecosystem with BantuHub; oil-dependent economy, little venture capital.
notes: FIGA guarantee fund site returned server error; omitted.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; non-EU founders use the standard long-stay D/AC business visa and residence permit)
company_setup: SRL (limited liability) registered with ONRC (Trade Register), typically a few days; foreigners can incorporate remotely via notarised power of attorney; low minimum share capital; micro-enterprise tax regime available.
summary: One of the largest tech talent pools in CEE, with hubs in Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, Iasi and Timisoara. UiPath is the flagship exit-scale success; VC supply grew sharply via the PNRR Recovery Equity Fund of Funds (EUR 380M allocated to 20 funds by mid-2026).
notes: As of 2026-10-20 no 2026 Start-Up Nation call was confirmed (industry groups were lobbying for one). PNRR Recovery Equity Fund of Funds (EIF) finished allocating EUR 380M to 20 VC/PE funds in June 2026; a successor EIF/BID fund of funds is planned from 2027. EBRD Star Venture coverage of Romania not confirmed, so omitted.

company_setup: LLC (OOO) registered with the Federal Tax Service, typically in days; foreigners can incorporate but face sanctions, capital controls and banking restrictions. Skolkovo participant status gives tax benefits for tech companies.
summary: Large domestic market with big tech groups (Yandex, VK, Sber, MTS, Ozon) and state-led innovation infrastructure (Skolkovo, Moscow Innovation Cluster, Innopolis, Kazan IT Park). Since 2022 the ecosystem has become largely domestic and state- or corporate-funded, after foreign VCs exited.
notes: Sanctions: Russia is under extensive US, EU, UK and other sanctions since 2014 and especially since February 2022; RDIF (RVC's parent since 2021), Skolkovo Foundation and Rusnano are on Western sanctions lists, and dealings with them may be prohibited for Western persons. International VCs, accelerators (YC, Techstars) and EU/EBRD programmes are unavailable; many founders relocated abroad. Several official sites (e.g. fasie.ru, sber500) block foreign access, so FASIE programme details could not be verified. Amounts converted at about RUB 80 per USD.

startup_visa: none dedicated; investor/entrepreneur permits via Rwanda Development Board, https://rdb.rw/
company_setup: Online registration with RDB Office of the Registrar General, often same day, free or low cost; foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Small but policy-driven ecosystem in Kigali with strong government support (RDB, MINICT), Norrsken House Kigali and Kigali Innovation City under development; strong in fintech, healthtech and govtech.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. BDF (Business Development Fund) left out: bdf.rw did not resolve (NXDOMAIN), so no official URL could be confirmed. Kigali Innovation City has no dedicated live site; listed via Africa50 project page. Hanga PitchFest site has a TLS certificate error.

company_setup: Company registered online with the Samoa Companies Registry. Foreign investors need a Foreign Investment Certificate from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
summary: Very small ecosystem in Apia built around tourism, agri-exports and remittance-linked digital services, with business support from government and the chamber of commerce.
notes: No local accelerators or VCs could be verified. The Small Business Enterprise Centre (SBEC) website was unreachable, so it is left out. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

startup_visa: none (residence for founders of certified high-tech startups available via San Marino Innovation certification)
company_setup: SRL or SpA; high-tech startup certification via San Marino Innovation gives simplified setup and tax benefits; local registered office required.
summary: Microstate ecosystem led by San Marino Innovation Institute, which certifies high-tech startups (with tax incentives) and hosts incubators; closely tied to the Italian market.
notes: Not in EU/Horizon Europe; no local VC found. Founders typically access Italian funding.

company_setup: OHADA company via the Guiché Único para Empresas (fast, low cost). Diaspora route: incorporate in Portugal.
summary: Micro-state with no formal startup ecosystem; Portuguese-speaking; relies on donor and pan-African programmes.
notes: No national startup programmes verified.

startup_visa: Entrepreneur licence via Ministry of Investment (MISA) plus Premium Residency entrepreneur category, https://misa.gov.sa/
company_setup: LLC with MISA licence for foreign owners (100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors), commercial registration via Saudi Business Center; 1-4 weeks.
summary: MENA's largest VC market by funding since 2023, centred on Riyadh, driven by Vision 2030, SVC fund-of-funds and Monsha'at; strengths in fintech, e-commerce, logistics and AI. Notable: Tabby, Tamara, Jahez IPO.
notes: monshaat.gov.sa and misk.org.sa block non-Saudi traffic; content verified via search results. Monsha'at programs run in cohorts with no published deadlines found.

company_setup: OHADA SARL or SAS via APIX one-stop shop (fast, low cost). Labelled startups get a 3-year tax exemption and 5% public-tender preference.
summary: Dakar is a leading francophone hub (Wave, InTouch); Startup Act (2020) relaunched in Nov 2025 with a national label portal; DER/FJ announced a US$50M pre-seed/seed fund in June 2026.
notes: Catalyst DER/FJ fund (US$50M) announced 2026-06-20 at VivaTech; application process not yet published. APIX site unreachable at time of check.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; foreign company owners use the type D visa for foreign company owners and a temporary residence/work permit, https://welcometoserbia.gov.rs)
company_setup: d.o.o. with minimum capital RSD 100, registered with the Business Registers Agency (APR), typically about 5 working days; electronic registration available with a qualified e-signature. Foreigners can fully own a company and register via a local proxy.
summary: Largest startup ecosystem in the Western Balkans, centred on Belgrade and Novi Sad with strong engineering talent and gaming/AI strengths. Exits include Nordeus (Take-Two), 3Lateral (Epic Games) and Frame (Microsoft); the Innovation Fund of Serbia is the main public funder.
notes: As of 2026-10-20: Smart Start 6th call open until 2026-11-16 12:00 (portal registration closes 2026-11-13). AI voucher intake temporarily paused since 2026-09-10 due to demand (call nominally runs to 2027-03-31). Katapult 6th call closed 2026-10-14. Mini Grants, Matching Grants and Serbia Ventures calls are closed.

company_setup: Domestic company or IBC via the Seychelles Financial Services Authority / Registrar; IBCs are popular with foreign founders.
summary: Small island economy built on tourism, fisheries and offshore finance; blue-economy innovation funding through SeyCCAT.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. SEnPA site not found.

company_setup: Company limited by shares via the Corporate Affairs Commission (online); SLIEPA assists foreign investors.
summary: Freetown ecosystem driven by DSTI and Freetown Innovation Week; Startup Act enacted per government (2026); Redsalt angel network launched Dec 2025.
notes: Sierra Leone Innovation Investment Fund (blended finance) in preparation; no URL verified.

startup_visa: EntrePass (Ministry of Manpower) for venture-backed or innovative founders, https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/entrepass ; ONE Pass for top talent
company_setup: Private limited (Pte Ltd) registered online with ACRA via BizFile+ in about a day, roughly S$315 in fees; foreigners need a locally resident director, usually via a corporate secretary or nominee service, so remote incorporation is possible.
summary: Southeast Asia's main startup and VC hub, home to most regional fund HQs and many unicorns (Grab, Sea, Carousell, Ninja Van). Strong government co-investment via Startup SG, EDB, SEEDS Capital and SGInnovate, plus deep-tech spinouts from NUS, NTU and A*STAR.
notes: Startup SG Tech caps were reported differently by secondary sources in 2026 (S$250k/500k vs S$400k/800k); confirm on Enterprise Singapore. Entrepreneur First no longer lists a Singapore office as of Oct 2026. WebSearch budget ran out mid-research, so some deadlines are patterns, not dates.

startup_visa: No dedicated startup visa verified; temporary residence for business purposes applies.
company_setup: s.r.o., EUR 5,000 minimum capital; online registration possible with Slovak eID, otherwise via notary or lawyer, about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Small ecosystem centred on Bratislava and Kosice; known names include Sygic, Pixel Federation and InoBat. Slovak Investment Holding is the main public co-investor, now making direct convertible-loan investments.
notes: SIH-backed VC funds (Vision Ventures, CBIM, Zero Gravity, Neulogy) have ended investment periods and are divesting per SIH; new fund status unconfirmed. SBA services partly down after cyber incident (Oct 2026).

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; non-EU founders apply for a single residence and work permit as company owners/representatives via the administrative units, https://e-uprava.gov.si/en)
company_setup: d.o.o. (LLC) with minimum capital EUR 7,500, registered free of charge through the SPOT/e-VEM portal or a SPOT point, typically 1-3 days. Non-residents need a Slovenian tax number and usually a notary or SPOT point visit; no full remote-incorporation route.
summary: Small but well-organised ecosystem centred on Ljubljana and Maribor, anchored by the Slovene Enterprise Fund's P2/SK75/SI-SK ladder and the Start:up Slovenia initiative. Known exits and success stories include Outfit7, Celtra, Bitstamp and Chipolo; PODIM in Maribor is the region's main startup conference.
notes: As of 2026-10-20: SEF site (podjetniskisklad.si) is behind bot verification, so exact 2027 tender dates for P2/SK75 could not be read; P2 2026 call was announced for February 2026. Slovenian Technology Fund (extra EUR 10M, managed by Silicon Gardens and Tivoli Partners) reported Dec 2025. Silverline Capital and RSG Capital excluded (placeholder or repurposed domains).

company_setup: Company registered online with the Company Haus registry. Foreign investors register with Invest Solomons.
summary: Small, mostly resource- and agriculture-based economy in Honiara with few formal startup structures; business support comes through government and donor programmes.
notes: No local accelerators or VCs could be verified. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

company_setup: Registration with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; many diaspora founders incorporate abroad (e.g. Kenya, UAE, US).
summary: Fragile-state ecosystem in Mogadishu with active mobile money (EVC Plus) and diaspora-funded businesses; hubs exist but few have stable websites.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Security and sanctions risks apply. SomInvest and iRise Hub domains did not resolve and were left out.

company_setup: Registration with Somaliland Ministry of Trade; recognition issues limit banking and foreign investment, so founders often incorporate abroad.
summary: Self-declared state, not internationally recognised; Hargeisa has a small ecosystem driven by mobile money (Zaad) and NGOs such as Shaqodoon.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Not recognised; iso2 'XS' is a placeholder (no ISO code). World Bank and UN programmes run through Somalia.

startup_visa: none (Startup Act SA campaign advocates one; founders use the business or critical-skills visa), https://www.dha.gov.za/
company_setup: Private company (Pty) Ltd registered online with CIPC, usually in days at low cost; foreigners can incorporate, local bank account and BEE rules matter.
summary: Africa's most mature ecosystem, centred on Cape Town and Johannesburg; strong in fintech, e-commerce, SaaS and climate; notable exits include Thawte, Takealot and PayFast.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. SEFA and SEDA were merged into SEDFA. The sefa.org.za and sedfa.org.za servers timed out from the checker, so the SEDFA URL is the official domain but its page could not be loaded. The R&D tax incentive (s11D) is a deduction, not a cash refund, so it is not listed as a grant.

startup_visa: D-8-4 Technology Startup visa through the OASIS points program (Ministry of Justice), plus the Startup Korea Special Visa track for founders selected through government programs such as KSGC. https://www.hikorea.go.kr
company_setup: Chusik Hoesa (stock company). Foreign investment is registered through KOTRA / Invest Korea, and KRW 100M or more of investment is needed for the D-8 investor visa. Incorporation takes about 1-3 weeks. Remote setup is possible through an agent with apostilled documents.
summary: Large, heavily state-backed ecosystem centred on Seoul (Gangnam, Pangyo), with the TIPS and KVIC fund-of-funds model at its core. Strong in AI, semiconductors, gaming, beauty and content. Unicorns include Toss, Danggeun and Musinsa, and Coupang listed on NYSE.
notes: KSGC 2026 ran May 6 to June 17, 2026. The next call (KSGC 2027) is expected around May-June 2027 but is not yet published. The old k-startupgc.org domain now hosts unrelated content, so use ksgc.global. TIPS rules changed in 2026: R&D ceiling KRW 800M and operator minimum KRW 200M, per press reports. Most government calls are published in the K-Startup integrated announcement each January.

company_setup: Registration with the Ministry of Justice business registry; high risk and limited banking; diaspora founders often incorporate in Kenya or Uganda.
summary: Fragile, conflict-affected economy; small Juba ecosystem supported mostly by donor programmes like Orange Corners and Inkomoko.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Ongoing instability; no investment authority website could be confirmed.

startup_visa: International entrepreneur residence under Ley 14/2013 and the Startups Law (Ley 28/2022), with ENISA certification for emerging companies, https://www.enisa.es/servicios/certificacion/
company_setup: SL with €1 minimum capital; NIE required for foreign founders; online formation via CIRCE/PAE in about 1–3 weeks; ENISA-certified startups get reduced corporate tax.
summary: Fast-growing ecosystem led by Madrid and Barcelona, with Valencia and Málaga rising. The 2022 Startups Law added tax breaks and a digital nomad/entrepreneur visa; strengths in fintech, mobility, travel tech and health; notable companies include Glovo, Cabify, Wallapop and TravelPerk.
notes: NEOTEC 2026 window ran 14 Apr–14 May 2026 (annual, usually spring). ENISA's former Jóvenes Emprendedores line is no longer listed. Some sites (Barcelona Activa, Demium, Tetuan Valley, Samaipartners) were unreachable and left out. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

company_setup: Private limited company via Registrar of Companies eROC online; 100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors; BOI registration for incentives; about 1-2 weeks.
summary: Small ecosystem centred on Colombo with strong IT/BPO talent; recovering from the 2022 economic crisis. Notable startups include PickMe and Kapruka.
notes: As of 2026-10-20. Lanka Angel Network, Blue Chip Venture Capital and Startup Sri Lanka sites could not be verified and were left out; local VC activity is thin.

company_setup: Company under the Companies Act (St Kitts) or a Nevis LLC/IBC (common offshore vehicle, formed remotely through agents).
summary: Micro ecosystem; finance comes from the Development Bank of St Kitts and Nevis, and SKIPA promotes investment. Citizenship by Investment brings foreign capital.
notes: OECS member, not an IDB borrowing member; regional support comes via CDB, Compete Caribbean, OECS and Caribbean Export. OECS Youth Empowerment Project small grants (US$5k) closed 2026-08-14.

company_setup: Company under the Companies Act via the Registry of Companies; foreign ownership allowed; CBI includes enterprise projects.
summary: Micro ecosystem. The Saint Lucia Development Bank runs a Youth Enterprises Equity Fund and Invest Saint Lucia promotes investment. Covered by the 2024 World Bank OECS entrepreneurship project.
notes: OECS member, not an IDB borrowing member; regional support comes via CDB, Compete Caribbean, OECS and Caribbean Export. OECS Youth Empowerment Project small grants (US$5k) closed 2026-08-14.

company_setup: Company under the Companies Act via CIPO; IBCs/LLCs available; foreign ownership allowed.
summary: Micro ecosystem; Invest SVG offers startup and new-venture support. No local accelerators or VCs.
notes: OECS member, not an IDB borrowing member; regional support comes via CDB, Compete Caribbean, OECS and Caribbean Export. OECS Youth Empowerment Project small grants (US$5k) closed 2026-08-14. The Centre for Enterprise Development (ced.vc) site did not resolve in Oct 2026.

company_setup: Registrar General of Commercial Registration; the war has disrupted registration and banking, so founders mostly incorporate abroad (e.g. Egypt, UAE).
summary: Pre-2023 Khartoum ecosystem largely displaced by the civil war; activity continues through diaspora and remote programmes.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Civil war since April 2023; US sanctions history; international VC effectively unavailable. 249Startups site was down (HTTP 526).

company_setup: NV (naamloze vennootschap) via notary and KKF (Chamber of Commerce) registration; foreigners can own; several weeks.
summary: Micro ecosystem in Paramaribo. The World Bank-funded SURGE programme gives matching grants to growth SMEs, and the Ministry of Economic Affairs (EZ) promotes ICT and FabLab initiatives. Expected oil revenue from 2028 may lift investment.
notes: Dutch is the business language. No local VC found; the KMO (SME) fund was relaunched but has no verified page.

startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; non-EU founders use the self-employment residence permit from Migrationsverket), https://www.migrationsverket.se/
company_setup: Aktiebolag (AB), minimum share capital SEK 25,000; registered with Bolagsverket via verksamt.se, online registration needs Swedish e-ID (BankID), otherwise paper filing; typically 1-2 weeks.
summary: Europe's most prolific unicorn producer per capita, centred on Stockholm with hubs in Gothenburg, Malmo/Lund and Uppsala. Strong in fintech, gaming, music tech, impact and deep tech; exits include Skype, Mojang, King, Klarna (IPO) and Spotify.
notes: Vinnova call list could not be parsed on 2026-10-20; check calls overview for live startup calls and deadlines. Sting autumn 2026 cohort already started; next intake date not published.

startup_visa: none (non-EU founders need a cantonal permit for self-employment, granted case by case)
company_setup: GmbH (CHF 20k capital) or AG (CHF 100k, CHF 50k paid in); notarised deed and commercial register entry; a Swiss-resident signatory is required; via EasyGov; 1–3 weeks.
summary: Highly research-driven ecosystem anchored by ETH Zurich and EPFL, with hubs in Zurich, Lausanne, Geneva, Basel and Zug. Strengths in deep tech, medtech, biotech, robotics, fintech and crypto; notable companies include On, Scandit, GetYourGuide and Climeworks.
notes: Venture Kick amount from established programme structure (CHF 10k/40k/100k); official page could not be read due to a cookie wall. MassChallenge Switzerland page blocks automated reads; deadline unknown. EIC Accelerator: remaining 2026 full-proposal cut-off is 4 Nov 2026; short proposals accepted any time; 2027 cut-offs not yet published (2027 info day 19 Nov 2026). EIC Pathfinder Open 2027 deadline awaits the 2027 Work Programme.

company_setup: Companies register via the Ministry of Economy; banking links remain limited. Most founders use a diaspora entity (UAE, Turkey, Estonia e-Residency, Delaware).
summary: Tiny, fragile ecosystem emerging after the Dec 2024 change of government; most Syrian founders operate from Turkey, Jordan, the Gulf or Europe. Reconstruction and diaspora returns are early signals.
notes: Sanctions: US lifted most Syria sanctions in mid-2025 and the EU eased economic sanctions, but compliance risk, de-risking by banks and conflict persist. No verified active accelerators or VCs inside Syria as of Oct 2026.

startup_visa: Entrepreneur Visa (MOEA Department of Investment Review) and the Employment Gold Card for qualified professionals, https://goldcard.nat.gov.tw
company_setup: Company limited by shares or limited company. Foreign investment needs prior approval from MOEA's Department of Investment Review and a local agent or address. No general minimum capital, though it must cover costs, and NT$6M is needed if sponsoring an Entrepreneur Visa through the investment route. Takes about 3-6 weeks.
summary: Hardware and semiconductor powerhouse with a growing software, AI and deep-tech startup scene centred on Taipei, Hsinchu and Kaohsiung. The government brand Startup Island TAIWAN and the National Development Fund co-invest heavily. Gogoro and Appier are the best-known exits.
notes: The NDF site (df.gov.tw) blocks automated fetches, so program amounts were not confirmed. The Taiwan Startup Stadium homepage looked partly outdated in Oct 2026. The Department of Investment Review site could not be reached from the research environment. Web search was exhausted during research.

company_setup: LLC registered via a single window at the tax committee, typically in a few days. Foreigners can own 100%. Remote incorporation is not established.
summary: Nascent ecosystem centred on Dushanbe and Khujand. Support comes mainly from donor and development programs such as the Aga Khan network's Accelerate Prosperity, with little local VC.
notes: Oct 2026: no government startup grant scheme or local VC could be verified. itpark.tj is a parked domain.

startup_visa: none; investor permits via Tanzania Investment Centre, https://www.tic.go.tz/
company_setup: Private company via BRELA online registration system; foreigners can incorporate, TIC certificate for incentives.
summary: Dar es Salaam-led ecosystem with hubs like Smart Lab, Sahara Ventures and Anza; fintech and agritech lead; COSTECH and UNDP Funguo provide early funding.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Buni Hub was unreachable and Tanzania Angels Alliance could not be verified, so both were left out.

startup_visa: SMART Visa (S category for startup founders, endorsed by NIA/depa/other agencies), https://smart-visa.boi.go.th/ ; Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa also available
company_setup: Private limited company registered with DBD; foreign majority ownership is limited by the Foreign Business Act unless BOI promotion or a Foreign Business Licence is obtained. Takes about 1–3 weeks; a local lawyer is usually needed.
summary: Bangkok-centred ecosystem with strong corporate venture activity from banks and conglomerates (SCB, Kasikorn, Krungsri, PTT) and agencies NIA and depa. Notable companies include Flash Express, Ascend Money and LINE MAN Wongnai.
notes: depa site blocks automated checks; 2026 Digital Startup Fund round details not confirmed. Thai Venture Capital Association site could not be resolved and is omitted.

company_setup: Company registration through SERVE (one-stop shop), usually within days; foreign investment guided by TradeInvest Timor-Leste. The economy uses the US dollar.
summary: Very small ecosystem in Dili supported mainly by government agencies and donors (UNDP, KOICA, ADB, World Bank). Timor-Leste joined ASEAN in 2025, and a government business incubation centre in Dili broke ground in January 2026.
notes: No local VC found. Diaspora founders often use Australian or Singapore entities.

company_setup: OHADA SARL/SAS via CFE one-stop shop (fast, online options). Diaspora founders often incorporate abroad with a local subsidiary.
summary: Lomé ecosystem of about 300 startups led by mobility/fintech super-app Gozem; government digital agenda via Agence Togo Digital; early-stage capital scarce.
notes: CCI-Togo startup investment fund planned for 2026; launch not confirmed. Agence Togo Digital site unreachable.

company_setup: Company registered with the Tonga Business Registries Office; foreign investors register under the Foreign Investment Act.
summary: Very small ecosystem in Nuku'alofa centred on agriculture, fisheries, tourism and remittances; startup support mostly comes through development banks and donors.
notes: The Ministry of Trade site blocked verification. The Tonga Business Enterprise Centre website could not be reached, so it is left out. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

company_setup: Private limited company registered online via TTBizLink (Companies Registry). Foreigners may incorporate; land ownership needs a licence. About 1-2 weeks.
summary: Energy-driven economy with a small tech scene in Port of Spain. Government support is mostly MSME grants and loans (SEED, NEDCO) plus the Ministry of Trade's Scale Up accelerator. Angel and VC activity is thin; the IDB is piloting CARIBEquity 'Ignite the World' here.
notes: idea2Innovation and the Tech Beach TBR Lab could not be confirmed active in 2025-26, so they are left out. The CARIBEquity pilot was approved Nov 2025.

startup_visa: none dedicated; Startup Act eases hiring foreigners and FX for labelled startups
company_setup: SARL/SUARL via Registre National des Entreprises; can be done in about a week; Startup Act label gives tax and FX benefits.
summary: Pioneer of the 2018 Startup Act (label, salary support, founder leave), with Tunis as hub; strong engineering talent and exits like InstaDeep (BioNTech).
notes: Last dated label session notice found: Oct 2025.

startup_visa: Turkiye Tech Visa (founders and tech talent), https://www.turkiyetechvisa.gov.tr/
company_setup: Ltd. Sti. or A.S. via trade registry; 100% foreign ownership allowed; about 1 week; technopark companies get tax exemptions.
summary: Large ecosystem led by Istanbul with Ankara and Izmir; gaming is a standout (Peak, Dream Games, Rollic), plus fintech and e-commerce (Getir, Trendyol). Strong state grants via TUBITAK and KOSGEB and 90+ technoparks.
notes: Lira volatility makes TRY amounts shrink in US$. BiGG+ Tohum window 5 Oct - 20 Nov 2026 reported via search; confirm on PRODIS.

company_setup: Business entities register with the Ministry of Finance and Economy, with local presence required. Foreign founders face visa and currency-conversion restrictions. Remote incorporation is not available, so founders usually incorporate abroad.
summary: Very small, state-dominated private sector with no visible startup or VC ecosystem. Restricted internet and a tightly controlled currency regime limit tech entrepreneurship.
notes: Oct 2026: no national startup agency, grants or VCs could be verified. Government sites were unreachable. EBRD Star Venture covers Central Asia, but Turkmenistan's eligibility in any given call should be confirmed.

company_setup: Business licensing goes through the government and island councils; the Tuvalu National Private Sector Organisation advises.
summary: Micro-economy with a very small private sector. The government's Digital Nation initiative is the main technology focus; there is no formal startup ecosystem.
notes: Government websites could not be reached, so no national SME agency URL could be verified. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

startup_visa: none; investment licence via Uganda Investment Authority, https://www.ugandainvest.go.ug/
company_setup: Private limited company via URSB online registration; foreigners can incorporate, typically within a week.
summary: Growing Kampala-centred ecosystem with hubs such as Outbox, Innovation Village and Hive Colab; strong in agritech, fintech and health; government STI Secretariat runs innovation funding.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Search quota ran out; StartUp Uganda and Uganda Angels domains were unreachable or parked and were left out.

company_setup: LLC (TOV) or sole proprietor (FOP); online registration via Diia for residents, foreigners usually register via a notary or representative. IT firms can join the Diia.City special regime (9% tax on withdrawn capital or 18% CIT, 5% PIT for staff). Many founders also use a Delaware, UK, Polish or Estonian parent.
summary: Large engineering talent base centred on Kyiv, Lviv, Kharkiv and Dnipro; known for Grammarly, GitLab (co-founded), MacPaw and Preply. Since 2022 the ecosystem has pivoted strongly to defence tech, supported by the state Brave1 cluster and a wave of defence-focused funds.
notes: Wartime context (since Feb 2022): martial law, power and security risks; defence tech dominates new funding. Seeds of Bravery (EIC-funded) has concluded. Star Venture Ukraine intake deadline 2026-10-30 per EU Neighbours East notice. USF Startup EDGE page says next call coming soon. EIC 2027 cut-offs to be published 2026-11-19. Several VC check sizes come from secondary sources.

startup_visa: Golden Visa (entrepreneur and skilled categories, 5-10 years), https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/residence-visas/golden-visa
company_setup: Free-zone LLC (DIFC, ADGM, DMCC, Hub71/ADGM, in5) or mainland LLC with 100% foreign ownership; can largely be done remotely in 1-3 weeks; US$3k-15k/year.
summary: MENA's leading startup hub (Dubai, Abu Dhabi) with heavy state support, free zones and global talent; notable exits Careem (Uber) and Souq (Amazon). Strong in fintech, AI and proptech.
notes: Hub71 Cohort 20 deadline (Aug 2026) has passed; Cohort 21 deadline Feb 2027 per site. in5, sme.ae, DIFC sites block bots but are official.

startup_visa: Innovator Founder visa (endorsement from an approved endorsing body, 3 years, settlement possible after 3 years), https://www.gov.uk/innovator-founder-visa; also Global Talent visa (digital technology route), https://www.gov.uk/global-talent
company_setup: Private limited company (Ltd) registered online with Companies House in about 24 hours for a £100 fee; non-residents can incorporate remotely but need a UK registered office address. SEIS/EIS advance assurance is standard before angel rounds.
summary: Europe's largest startup ecosystem, centred on London with strong clusters in Cambridge, Oxford, Manchester and Edinburgh; leads Europe in fintech, AI and deep tech. Notable successes include Arm, Revolut, Wise, DeepMind and Deliveroo.
notes: Innovate UK Smart grants closed to new applications in 2025; funding now goes through themed competitions (check the competition search). EIS limits rose to £10m a year and £24m lifetime from 6 April 2026. Wayra UK, Ignite and Oxford Foundry were left out because their current pages could not be verified. Many investor sites block automated checks but are active. Web search budget ran out mid-batch, so some deadlines are 'unknown'.

startup_visa: No dedicated startup visa. International Entrepreneur Parole (IER, Form I-941, needs ~US$311k qualified investment or ~US$124k government grant; DHS has signalled rescission), plus O-1, H-1B, E-2 and EB-5 routes. https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/international-entrepreneur-rule
company_setup: Delaware C-corp is standard for VC-backed startups. Foreigners can incorporate remotely (e.g. Stripe Atlas, Clerky) for a few hundred US$ in 1-3 days; EIN and US bank account are possible without residency.
summary: Largest startup ecosystem in the world, centered on the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, Boston, Los Angeles, Austin and Seattle. It leads in AI, software, biotech and defense tech, with the deepest VC market and exits such as Google, Meta, Uber, Airbnb and OpenAI's growth.
notes: SBIR/STTR lapsed 2025-10-01 and was reauthorized 2026-04-13 through 2031-09-30; agencies are still rebuilding solicitation calendars. DoD FY27 Release 1 opens 2026-10-28 and closes 2026-11-25 (from secondary source). International Entrepreneur Parole remains on USCIS site but rescission has been signalled. Web search budget ran out mid-research, so some state programs (Colorado, Maryland TEDCO, NY) were left out and some accelerator deadlines remain unknown; VC check sizes left as unknown.

startup_visa: none (no startup visa; SprintUY by ANII/Uruguay XXI supports foreign startups relocating; residence is straightforward)
company_setup: Typical entity S.A.S. (since 2019), can be set up quickly online; foreigners can incorporate with a local address and RUT; about 1–3 weeks.
summary: Small but high-output ecosystem in Montevideo with strong software exports; dLocal is the main unicorn exit. ANII and Uruguay XXI run permanent startup support and soft-landing programs.
notes: ANII lists eight permanent calls as of Oct 2026 but the listing does not state amounts; check each bases document. ~UYU 40/US$.

startup_visa: No startup visa. Uzbekistan offers an IT visa for IT specialists, IT company owners and investors through IT Park, https://outsource.gov.uz/
company_setup: LLC registered via the one-stop shop in about 1-3 days. 100% foreign ownership allowed. IT Park residents pay 0% corporate tax, 0% social payments and 7.5% personal income tax.
summary: Fast-growing ecosystem anchored by IT Park in Tashkent and the state fund of funds UzVC. Strengths are IT outsourcing, fintech and edtech. Uzum is the best-known tech company.
notes: Oct 2026: no dated open accelerator calls found. The innovation ministry site (mininnovation.uz) returned 502 and is left out. UzVC also backs Big Sky Capital Fund II and Sarmo.

company_setup: Company registered with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission. Foreign investors need approval from the Vanuatu Foreign Investment Promotion Agency (VFIPA).
summary: Small ecosystem in Port Vila built around tourism, agriculture and offshore finance services, with limited formal startup support.
notes: No local accelerators or VCs could be verified. Most Pacific founders raise from Australian or NZ investors and often incorporate there; check PTI and ADB programmes for current calls.

company_setup: Not possible for private founders; founders use Italy (Rome) instead.
summary: No startup ecosystem: the state has no private company formation for outsiders, no accelerators, VCs or startup grants. Listed for completeness only.
notes: No startup ecosystem; see Italy for nearby resources.

company_setup: Compania Anonima (C.A.) registered at the Registro Mercantil (SAREN) plus RIF tax ID; slow and bureaucratic. Many founders incorporate in the US or Delaware.
summary: Small, recovering ecosystem in Caracas. A 2026 market map counts about 105 active startups. Casa212 offers a US$150k founder residency, the first Venezuela Tech Week ran in May 2026, and the Startup Venezuela Summit runs 2026-10-21 to 23.
notes: US sanctions (OFAC) on the government and PDVSA complicate dealings with state entities and banking, as of Oct 2026. Most founders use offshore holding companies. Venezuela is an IDB member but IDB lending has been frozen for years. The FONACIT site was unreachable.

company_setup: Foreign founders typically set up a single-member LLC with an Investment Registration Certificate then Enterprise Registration Certificate; takes about 1–2 months. Many startups use a Singapore holding company for fundraising.
summary: Fast-growing ecosystem in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi with strong engineering talent; notable companies include VNG, MoMo, Sky Mavis and VNLife. Government backing via the National Innovation Center (NIC) and the National Technology Innovation Fund.
notes: SIHUB (Ho Chi Minh City) and Nextrans sites could not be resolved in Oct 2026 and are omitted. No startup visa; foreign-owned company setup is slow.

company_setup: In Moroccan-administered areas, companies register under Moroccan law via regional investment centres.
summary: Disputed territory; the Moroccan-administered areas (Laayoune, Dakhla) follow Moroccan programs; essentially no startup ecosystem in Polisario-held areas.
notes: Sovereignty disputed (UN non-self-governing territory); Moroccan national programs (Tamwilcom, Maroc PME) apply in administered areas. EU court rulings affect trade.

company_setup: Registration is split between rival authorities; most founders use a diaspora entity (Saudi, UAE, Estonia e-Residency, Delaware).
summary: Fragile, conflict-affected economy with a very small number of tech startups, mostly in Sanaa and Aden; support comes from donor-funded small-business programs.
notes: Ongoing civil war and Red Sea crisis; US sanctions and FTO designation of Ansar Allah (Houthis) complicate payments. No verified active VCs or accelerators.

startup_visa: none; investor permits via Zambia Development Agency, https://zda.org.zm/
company_setup: Private limited company via PACRA online registration; foreigners can incorporate.
summary: Lusaka ecosystem anchored by BongoHive, with growing fintech and agritech; government CEEC provides citizen enterprise finance.

startup_visa: none; investment licence via ZIDA, https://zidainvest.com/
company_setup: Private limited company with the Companies Registry (online via ZIDA one-stop shop); currency and FX rules complicate fundraising.
summary: Harare-centred ecosystem shaped by mobile money (EcoCash) and currency instability; strong technical talent and a large diaspora.
notes: Checked 2026-10-20. Currency volatility (ZiG) and FX controls. No local accelerator site could be confirmed live; zida.co.zw is a placeholder, so zidainvest.com is used.
